nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which the power asymmetry between corporate entities profiting from LLMs and other social groups makes LLM governance protocols excessively favourable to technology companies, leading to regulatory capture at the cost of other societal groups, particularly marginalised communities.

nodes.name: Global AI supply chain disruption
nodes.definition: The risk that unilateral coercive measures such as technology barriers and export restrictions maliciously disrupt the highly globalised AI supply chain, causing significant supply disruptions for chips, software, and tools.

nodes.name: Labour power asymmetry from algorithmic management
nodes.name_ko: 알고리즘 관리에 따른 노동 권력 비대칭
nodes.definition: The risk that algorithmic management through AI-based performance scoring, work allocation, or behavioural control concentrates information and control in employers or platform operators, weakens workers' bargaining power, collective capacity, and ability to challenge managerial decisions, and deepens workplace power asymmetry and inequality.

nodes.name: Erosion of human decision-making capacity and veto
nodes.definition: The risk that organisational pressure, interface design, automation speed, and habitual reliance on AI weaken users' capacity to deliberate and choose under uncertainty and to veto consequential AI recommendations, leaving harmful outputs effectively uncontested.

nodes.name: Loss of due process in automated decisions
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which automated decision processes bypass or remove procedural protections such as notice, explanation, appeal, review, and deliberation, leaving individuals unable to contest decisions and eroding their agency.

nodes.name: Alert fatigue in AI decision support
nodes.definition: The risk that frequent or poorly prioritised AI alerts cause users to ignore important warnings.

nodes.name: Failure to recognise a user's emotional context
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise or appropriately account for a vulnerable user's distress, emotional state, or reactions as relevant interaction context, producing emotionally inappropriate responses that undermine the user's well-being.

nodes.name: Honorific and politeness norm failure
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems fail to preserve honorific, politeness, hierarchy, or relational norms that carry ethical meaning in a language community.

nodes.name: Failure to recognise user capability and accessibility context
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise and account for a user's cognitive, linguistic, literacy, sensory, physical, or mobility capabilities and accessibility requirements as part of the interaction context, producing information, advice, or actions that the user cannot understand or use and thereby undermining safety and user interests.

nodes.name: Panic and anxiety from content that disregards emotional and situational context
nodes.name_ko: 정서·상황 맥락을 무시한 콘텐츠에 의한 공황·불안
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise and account for a user's emotional state, situation, or interaction context and generates or presents threatening, distressing, or inappropriate content that induces or aggravates panic, severe anxiety, or psychological distress.

nodes.name: AI evaluation failure under distribution shift
nodes.name_ko: 분포 변화에 대한 AI 평가·검증 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that evaluation of an AI system fails to detect performance degradation and confidence errors when test, training, and operational distributions differ, overstating real-world reliability and safety and leading to unsafe deployment decisions.

nodes.name: Assurance case failure
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which safety or assurance cases are incomplete, unverifiable, or not updated as systems and contexts change.

nodes.name: Benchmark limitations mismeasuring capability and safety
nodes.definition: The risk that saturated, incomplete, or overfitted benchmarks mismeasure AI systems, underestimating capabilities that lack test coverage, overestimating those tuned to benchmark contents, and lagging on safety and harm assessment, so developers and users acquire a false sense of the system's abilities, limitations, and safety.

nodes.name: Certification capture
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which certification or conformity assessment becomes influenced by vendor interests rather than public risk reduction, undermining the independence and objectivity of evaluations and preventing the effective identification and mitigation of real risks.

nodes.name: Deceptive behavioural change from evaluation awareness
nodes.name_ko: 평가 상황 인식에 따른 기만적 행동 변화
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system recognises whether it is in training, evaluation, or deployment and uses that situational awareness to behave safely only during evaluation or conceal dangerous capabilities or goals, while exhibiting dangerous behaviour when oversight is weaker in deployment, undermining evaluation validity and creating false assurance of safety.

nodes.name: Deficient data collection quality control
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which a lack of standardised methods, sufficient infrastructure, and quality-control processes for collecting data, especially for high-stakes domains and benchmarks, affects the quality and type of data collected, including dataset poisoning, inadvertent copyright violation, and test-set leakage that invalidates performance metrics.

nodes.name: Evaluation and measurement failure for long-term and diffuse AI harms
nodes.definition: The risk that evaluation and validation processes for an AI system fail to detect or measure harms that are subtle, diffuse, or emerge over long periods, creating unwarranted assurance about safety and leading to inappropriate deployment or governance decisions.

nodes.name: Failure of disclosure and change tracking for model flaws
nodes.definition: The risk that vulnerabilities, model failures, or harmful capabilities cannot be disclosed safely and acted upon, and that changes to model versions, data, or prompts are not tracked well enough to attribute new failures, leaving flaws unremedied and responsibility unassigned.

nodes.name: Failure of participatory and value-sensitive design
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems are developed and deployed without structured analysis of stakeholder values, value conflicts, and design tradeoffs, or without genuine representation of affected communities, embedding unexamined value choices that disserve those communities.

nodes.name: Failure to detect erroneous or harmful outputs in human evaluation
nodes.name_ko: 인간 평가에서 부정확하거나 유해한 출력의 식별 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that human evaluators cannot reliably distinguish subtly incorrect or harmful AI model outputs from correct outputs during feedback-based training and evaluate them positively, causing the model to learn to generate code with hidden software vulnerabilities, politically biased information, or complex outputs containing concealed errors or backdoors.

nodes.name: Failure to reassess safety after deployment changes
nodes.name_ko: 배포 후 변경에 대한 안전 재평가 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that operators fail to reassess and verify the safety of physical AI after environmental changes, component degradation, model updates, or near-miss incidents invalidate prior assumptions, allowing operation to continue on inadequate safety evidence.

nodes.name: Failure-mode ambiguity in agent incidents
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which agent incidents cannot be consistently classified by failure mode, making diagnosis, benchmark comparison, and mitigation selection unreliable.

nodes.name: False-negative safety evaluation of household robot actions
nodes.name_ko: 가정 내 로봇 행동 안전성 평가의 위음성
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI safety classifier incorrectly labels a proposed household robot action as safe despite violations of human-contact, heat, object, or workspace constraints, failing to detect hazardous behaviour and producing false safety assurance.

nodes.name: Fundamental-rights impact assessment gap
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems are deployed without adequate assessment of rights, discrimination, privacy, and democratic impacts.

nodes.name: Incomplete pre-deployment physical safety testing
nodes.name_ko: 배포 전 물리적 안전 시험 미흡
nodes.definition: The risk that a foundation-model-enabled robot is released without testing domain shifts, adversarial inputs, human contact, and safety-critical edge cases relevant to its intended environment.

nodes.name: Incorrect risk measurement and prediction
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which metrics selected to measure or track a risk capture it incompletely or target the wrong risk for the context, and that systems fail to make correct predictions, so decisions rest on inaccurate measurement and erroneous outputs.

nodes.name: Lack of metrics for evaluating AI-assistant benefits and harms
nodes.name_ko: AI 비서의 편익·피해 평가 지표 부재
nodes.definition: The risk that valid metrics for comprehensively measuring the benefits and harms of AI assistants to individuals and society are lacking, preventing reliable evaluation of the system's net effects and potential for harm.

nodes.name: Security test coverage gap in tool agents
nodes.name_ko: 도구 에이전트 보안 테스트 커버리지 격차
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which benchmarks omit realistic tool, application, or attack combinations, creating false confidence in tool-agent security.

nodes.name: Self-preference bias in model evaluation
nodes.definition: The risk that AI models are prone to self-preference bias, favouring their own generated content over that of others in self-evaluation tasks and model-based evaluations more broadly, resulting in unfair discrimination against human-generated content.

nodes.name: Truncated safety evaluation under competitive release pressure
nodes.name_ko: 경쟁 압력에 따른 안전성 평가 축소와 성급한 배포
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which competitive pressure leads developers to cut corners on safety evaluation while prioritising capabilities, so that GPAI systems are released without verifying risks correlated with those capabilities.

nodes.name: Over-assurance from insufficient auditor capacity
nodes.name_ko: 감사자 역량 부족에 따른 과대 보증
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which auditors lacking knowledge of specific risks or the capacity for sufficiently rigorous testing report passing audits more inclusive than can be justified.

nodes.name: Omission of rare conditions and vulnerable users from physical AI benchmarks
nodes.name_ko: 피지컬 AI 벤치마크의 희귀 조건·취약 사용자 누락
nodes.definition: The risk that benchmarks for physical AI systems fail to include rare combinations of objects, layouts, human behaviour, hazards, or conditions affecting vulnerable users, allowing systems that cannot safely detect, predict, or accommodate people under those conditions to remain unidentified during evaluation, be deployed, and cause unsafe physical action or injury.

nodes.name: Misinterpretation of object affordances and scenes
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system misunderstands the actions afforded by an object or the relationships in a scene, producing infeasible or unsafe judgements.

nodes.name: Degradation of the shared information ecosystem
nodes.name_ko: 공유 정보 생태계의 오염과 질 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which false, hallucinated, low-quality, or realistically fabricated depictions of people and events produced by generative tools circulate beyond the end user and contaminate publicly available information. People form inaccurate perceptions and decisions on that basis and lose trust even in accurate information.

nodes.name: Erroneous medical and scientific conclusions from data misinterpretation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system misuses medical or scientific data or misinterprets its context, quality, or uncertainty, producing unsupported or factually incorrect conclusions that distort research or clinical decision-making.

nodes.name: Factual errors injected by external tools
nodes.name_ko: 외부 도구에 의해 주입된 사실 오류
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which external tools incorporate additional knowledge from public resources such as web APIs and search engines into input prompts, and that unreliable tool content containing factual errors consequently amplifies the hallucination issue.

nodes.name: Failure to distinguish synthetic content and persistent harm
nodes.name_ko: 합성 콘텐츠의 진위 식별 실패와 지속적 피해
nodes.definition: The risk that AI generates realistic deepfakes or other synthetic content that recipients cannot reliably distinguish from authentic material, causing informational, social, or reputational harm that can persist even after the content is debunked.

nodes.name: False information targeting an individual
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates or disseminates false or fabricated information about an identifiable individual, causing harm to that person’s reputation, safety, rights, or social relationships.

nodes.name: Generation of false information about election procedures
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates or provides false information about voting eligibility, dates, locations, or procedures, misleading voters.

nodes.name: Generation of historically revisionist accounts
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system causes, enables, or contributes to deliberate or unintentional reinterpretation of established or orthodox historical events or accounts held by societies, communities, and academics.

nodes.name: Lowered barriers to large-scale disinformation production and dissemination
nodes.definition: The risk that AI cheaply produces synthetic media and false news at scale, blurs distinctions among fact, opinion, and fiction, and thereby expands the speed, scale, and targeting of disinformation production and dissemination.

nodes.name: Misinformation harms from algorithmic systems
nodes.name_ko: 알고리즘 시스템에 의한 허위·오도 정보 피해
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-based algorithmic systems, including generative models and recommender systems, generate, recommend, or amplify false, misleading, or unverified information, thereby distorting individual and societal understanding and decision-making.

nodes.name: Misleading medical information and unsafe medication guidance
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates or provides factually incorrect or insufficiently supported medical information or unsafe medication guidance, distorting a user's diagnostic or treatment decisions and causing harm to physical or mental health.

nodes.name: AI advice beyond validated professional scope
nodes.name_ko: 검증된 전문성 범위를 벗어난 AI 조언
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system provides medical, legal, financial, electoral, or safety advice beyond its validated capability, expertise, or authority and presents that advice as reliable, inducing misplaced trust, erroneous decisions, and material, legal, or physical harm.

nodes.name: Misrepresentation of autonomous learning and self-improvement capabilities
nodes.name_ko: 자율적 학습·자기 개선 역량의 허위 표상
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents itself as able to learn autonomously or improve itself beyond its validated capabilities, distorting user judgement or inducing misplaced trust or dependence.

nodes.name: Unjustified refusal of legitimate requests due to intent misclassification in safety controls
nodes.name_ko: 안전 통제의 사용자 의도 오분류에 따른 정당 요청 거부
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or agent misclassifies user intent during safety control and unjustifiably refuses legitimate requests, impeding users' legitimate goals and the utility of the service.

nodes.name: Denial of access to legitimate information due to exaggerated safety filtering
nodes.name_ko: 안전 필터의 과잉 차단에 따른 정당한 정보 접근 거부
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system refuses requests for safely providable information, such as medical, legal, educational, or emergency-response content, by misclassifying them as harmful based on sensitive wording or topical similarity, impeding users' right to know and legitimate access to information.

nodes.name: Over-refusal of help-seeking requests from vulnerable users
nodes.name_ko: 취약 이용자 지원 요청의 과잉 거절
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system categorically refuses help-seeking requests, such as suicide prevention, addiction recovery, or abuse response, because the topics are sensitive, leaving vulnerable users without timely supportive information and driving them toward unverified sources.

nodes.name: Excessive confidence under uncertainty
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents outputs with high confidence despite uncertainty or insufficient evidence, causing users to overestimate their reliability.

nodes.name: Moral uncertainty neglect
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems present a single confident moral judgement where uncertainty, disagreement, or deliberation would be appropriate.

nodes.name: Catastrophic forgetting under continual tuning
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system causes, enables, or contributes to catastrophic forgetting, where a model loses its ability to retain previously learned tasks or factual information after being trained on new ones, as can occur through continual instruction tuning, a tendency that may become more pronounced as the model's size increases.

nodes.name: Dataset shift between training and runtime data
nodes.definition: The risk that the training data and the testing or runtime data of an AI/ML model demonstrate different distributions, undermining the model's validity.

nodes.name: Over- and underfitting
nodes.definition: The risk that over- or underfitting, the excessive or insufficient adaptation of a model to training data, causes an AI system to behave unreliably when confronted with operational data.

nodes.name: Reliability and safety failure outside the validated operating envelope
nodes.name_ko: 검증된 운용 범위 밖에서의 신뢰성·안전성 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that complex operating environments produce situations unanticipated in design, undermining the reliability and safety of AI systems outside their validated envelope.

nodes.name: Failure of performance, robustness, and resilience under adverse conditions
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to fulfil its intended purpose and cannot maintain stable performance, or recover, when inputs are disturbed by malicious attack, data poisoning, environmental noise, or failures in connected components. Unreliable models and error-prone agents remain in operation, producing severe consequences for those who depend on them.

nodes.name: Model safety-performance degradation from fine-tuning
nodes.name_ko: 미세조정에 따른 모델 안전 성능 열화
nodes.definition: The risk that downstream fine-tuning on benign and commonplace data degrades an AI model's safety training and safety performance, increasing the likelihood of harmful or unreliable outputs relative to the base model.

nodes.name: Reliability and safety degradation from an inappropriate level of automation
nodes.name_ko: 부적절한 자동화 수준에 따른 신뢰성·안전성 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that the level of automation in an AI application is inappropriately high or low relative to its operating context and validated performance, causing unexpected behaviour, performance degradation, or failure of safety functions.

nodes.name: Reliability degradation from unexpected capability changes after fine-tuning
nodes.name_ko: 미세조정 후 예기치 않은 역량 변화에 따른 신뢰성 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that downstream fine-tuning of a general-purpose AI model produces capabilities or behavioural properties that were not previously validated, making performance boundaries and safety properties difficult to predict and causing unreliable or unsafe outputs in deployment.

nodes.name: Performance and service-reliability degradation from inadequate compute and power capacity planning
nodes.name_ko: 연산·전력 용량 계획 결함에 따른 성능·서비스 신뢰성 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that compute and power requirements for developing or operating an AI system are not adequately incorporated into hardware selection, capacity planning, or operational design, causing degraded processing performance, service interruption, or failure to meet safety requirements.

nodes.name: Safety-response failure from spikes in perception and inference latency
nodes.name_ko: 인지·추론 지연 급증에 따른 안전 대응 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that perception or inference latency in an AI system spikes during operation, preventing hazards from being detected, assessed, or addressed within required time limits and causing performance, reliability, or safety requirements to be missed.

nodes.name: Confidential information in training data disclosed through outputs
nodes.name_ko: 학습 데이터 내 기밀정보 포함과 출력 노출
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which confidential information is incorporated into training data, tuning data, or prompts and is subsequently reproduced in generated outputs. Such leakage exposes protected business and personal information to unauthorised parties and breaches confidentiality obligations.

nodes.name: Disclosure of confidential safety-policy and safeguard information
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system discloses, permits the inference or extraction of, or fails to protect confidential information about safety policies, filtering logic, refusal rules, or safeguard configuration and operation, compromising confidentiality and the effectiveness of security controls.

nodes.name: Disclosure of confidential business information and trade secrets
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system reproduces, infers, extracts, or discloses non-public research, technical information, business strategy, or trade secrets, or fails to protect such information, compromising confidentiality, intellectual-property rights, and legitimate economic interests.

nodes.name: Business harm from unauthorised sharing of confidential information
nodes.name_ko: 기밀정보 무단 공유에 따른 사업상 피해
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system shares non-public business strategy, financial plans, contracts, customer information, or operational information with unauthorised third parties or transmits it to external services, harming market position, bargaining power, revenue, or legal interests.

nodes.name: Agent goal hijacking through untrusted external instructions and intent
nodes.name_ko: 신뢰할 수 없는 외부 지시·의도에 의한 에이전트 목표 탈취
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent incorporates instructions or expressed intent from user input, external content, tool responses, or other actors into its goals or plans without validating authority and provenance, causing action that departs from the original task and safety constraints.

nodes.name: Agent identity and authority spoofing
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which an attacker impersonates a user, tool, service, or peer agent so that an agent accepts unauthorised instructions or trust relationships.

nodes.name: Automated discovery of jailbreaks through proxy-objective optimisation
nodes.name_ko: 프록시 목표 최적화를 통한 탈옥 자동 탐색
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which jailbreak attacks are discovered by performing manual or automated, gradient-based or gradient-free adversarial optimisation against a proxy objective noisily correlated with jailbreak success.

nodes.name: Backdoors or trojan attacks in GPAI models
nodes.name_ko: GPAI 모델의 백도어 또는 트로이 목마 공격
nodes.definition: The risk that backdoors inserted into GPAI models during training or fine-tuning, by the model provider or another actor manipulating training data or software infrastructure, are exploited during deployment to control model outputs in a targeted way with high success rate and minimal overhead.

nodes.name: Compromise of robot fleets
nodes.definition: The risk that attackers exploit vulnerabilities in cloud services, software updates, APIs, or orchestration layers to cause simultaneous unauthorised access to, manipulation of, or disruption of multiple AI-enabled robots, vehicles, drones, or industrial systems.

nodes.name: Cyber compromise of robotic systems in critical infrastructure
nodes.name_ko: 핵심 기반시설 로봇 시스템의 사이버 침해
nodes.definition: The risk that attackers exploit software or network vulnerabilities in robotic inspection, maintenance, logistics, or control systems used in critical infrastructure, causing unauthorised access, manipulation, or disruption and thereby impairing operations or damaging equipment.

nodes.name: Disruption of third-party systems
nodes.definition: The risk that generative AI facilitates the damage, disruption, or destruction of a third-party system and its components via malfunction, cyberattacks, and similar means.

nodes.name: Expanded attack surface in agent interfaces
nodes.definition: The risk that vulnerabilities or excessive privileges in interfaces connecting AI agents to browsers, operating systems, mobile applications, IoT devices, or external APIs create attack vectors through which attackers bypass safeguards, gain unauthorised access, cause manipulation or disruption, or induce unsafe actions.

nodes.name: Access to prohibited information or content through safeguard bypass
nodes.name_ko: 안전장치 우회를 통한 금지 정보·콘텐츠 접근
nodes.definition: The risk that an attacker uses jailbreaks, adversarially constructed instructions, or exposed safety policies or filtering rules to analyse, bypass, or disable an AI system's safeguards and gain access to prohibited information, content, or capabilities.

nodes.name: Ingestion of harmful content through external tool integration
nodes.name_ko: 외부 도구 연동을 통한 유해 콘텐츠 유입
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which growing integration and interconnectivity with external tools and plugins exposes a system to malicious external inputs that introduce harmful content.

nodes.name: Multi-step jailbreaks
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which multi-step jailbreaks, constructing well-designed scenarios across a series of conversations through request contextualising or external assistance, guide LLMs to generate harmful or sensitive content step by step.

nodes.name: Principal-information theft and action manipulation through attacks on delegate agents
nodes.name_ko: 위임 에이전트 공격에 의한 정보 탈취·행위 조작
nodes.definition: The risk that AI agents acting as delegates of humans or organisations become a novel attack surface, letting attackers extract private information about their principals, manipulate agents into undesired actions, subvert overseer agents, thwart cooperation, or leak information enabling collusion.

nodes.name: Safeguard bypass through persona, role-play, and social-engineering techniques
nodes.definition: The risk that an attacker assigns an AI system a particular persona or a harmful role, including extremist or racist roles, or uses social-engineering or role-play instructions to bypass safeguards and elicit prohibited outputs or actions.

nodes.name: Supply-chain compromise of AI tools and dependencies
nodes.definition: The risk that compromised software supply-chain elements, including external tools, plug-ins, APIs, packages, connectors, and development toolchain dependencies, introduce tampered components or vulnerabilities into an AI system, manipulating an agent's action space or exfiltrating information.

nodes.name: Unauthorised access, manipulation, and disruption of AI computing infrastructure
nodes.name_ko: AI 컴퓨팅 인프라의 무단 접근·조작·서비스 중단
nodes.definition: The risk that an attacker exploits vulnerabilities in AI computing infrastructure to gain unauthorised access to distributed nodes or services, manipulate configurations, data, or workloads, disrupt operations, or propagate compromise across system boundaries.

nodes.name: Propagation of foundation-model security vulnerabilities into unsafe physical action
nodes.name_ko: 기반 모델 보안 취약성의 위험한 물리 행동 전이
nodes.definition: The risk that safeguards in a foundation model integrated into a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system are bypassed or manipulated through jailbreaks, prompt injection, adversarial input, or other security compromise, and the resulting output propagates through planning and control into unsafe physical action.

nodes.name: Sensor spoofing and signal injection
nodes.definition: The risk that attackers spoof or inject GNSS, camera, lidar, radar, RFID, audio, tactile, or wireless sensor signals to manipulate an AI system's physical-state estimation and subsequent physical actions without authorisation.

nodes.name: Bias concealment through manipulated explanations
nodes.definition: The risk that existing explainability techniques are insufficient for detecting discriminatory biases and that manipulation methods hide underlying biases, generating misleading explanations that exclude sensitive attributes such as race or gender and do not accurately represent the underlying model.

nodes.name: Inadequate disclosure in AI interaction
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to adequately disclose the fact of AI interaction, its functions, limitations, or the basis of its outputs, impairing informed judgement.

nodes.name: Misleading representation of AI product capabilities
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI provider presents an AI system's functions, limitations, or validation scope in an unclear or misleading manner, impairing informed user judgement.

nodes.name: Overreliance on AI counterfactual explanations and liability misattribution
nodes.name_ko: AI 반사실적 설명의 과신과 책임 오귀속
nodes.definition: The risk that operators or regulators mistake an AI model's counterfactual explanation for verified causal evidence, obscuring the decision's limitations and uncertainty and leading to misattribution of responsibility.

nodes.name: User comprehension overload
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which system information, warnings, or explanations exceed users' ability to understand and act on them.

nodes.name: Robot performance and accessibility failure in public-space operation
nodes.name_ko: 공공 공간 운용에서의 로봇 성능·접근성 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that a service robot operating in public space fails to reliably meet path-planning, position-keeping, clear-passage, or accessibility requirements, blocking or encroaching on pavements, ramps, entrances, or navigation cues and restricting access for disabled people and other pedestrians.

nodes.name: Failure of robot collision avoidance and operating-zone control
nodes.definition: The risk that an autonomous mobile robot fails to comply with collision-avoidance, geofencing, or designated operating-zone constraints, causing collisions with people, facilities, or other vehicles or entering restricted areas.

nodes.name: Failure to detect or anticipate physical hazards around people
nodes.name_ko: 사람 주변의 물리적 위험 감지·예측 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that a multimodal or embodied AI system operating in a shared space fails to detect human presence, movement, contact, or environmental change in visual or sensor inputs, or to anticipate the resulting hazard, and selects an action that causes collision or injury.

nodes.name: Failure to detect precursors of rare injuries
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot, humanoid, or embodied AI system sharing space with people fails to detect precursors of rare but foreseeable falls, poisoning, burns, lacerations, or crush injuries and therefore fails to warn, stop, avoid, or intervene safely.

nodes.name: Failure to enforce human-robot physical safety rules
nodes.name_ko: 인간-로봇 물리 안전 규칙 집행 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that a constitutional safety layer in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system fails to prioritise human-robot safety rules, such as maintaining safe separation, stopping when a person is detected, or executing a safe handover, when user instructions, visual context, or task framing conflict with those rules, creating a hazardous situation.

nodes.name: Failure to provide required support or escalation in high-risk situations
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot, humanoid, or embodied AI system fails to provide assigned essential physical support in a high-risk situation or fails to escalate a detected hazard or need to a person or oversight system, leaving necessary support unavailable and compromising safety or dignity.

nodes.name: Human-robot safety failure in sim-to-real transfer
nodes.name_ko: 시뮬레이션-실세계 전이 과정의 인간-로봇 안전 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that a policy for a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system is trained or validated in simulations that do not adequately represent human movement, contact, or shared-space conditions, then fails to detect, anticipate, or accommodate people in real operation and creates hazardous situations after deployment under false safety assurance.

nodes.name: Inadequate human-contact safety controls
nodes.definition: The risk that safety controls fail to limit robot speed, force, distance, or contact during direct human interaction, exposing nearby people to collision or injury.

nodes.name: Missing safety context in demonstration learning
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot imitates a human demonstration without inferring unobserved safety conditions such as permitted force, excluded objects, or situational limits.

nodes.name: Physical disabling of safety interlocks and emergency stops
nodes.definition: The risk that an attacker physically tampers with, disables, or defeats hardware safety mechanisms of a robot or physical AI system, such as emergency stops, safety interlocks, and torque or speed limiters, eliminating harm-prevention functions and increasing the likelihood of injury or property damage.

nodes.name: Integrity compromise via physical theft or replacement of compute and storage modules
nodes.name_ko: 연산·저장 모듈의 물리적 탈취·교체에 의한 무결성 훼손
nodes.definition: The risk that an attacker with physical access steals, replaces, or modifies hardware components of a robot or physical AI system, such as control boards, storage devices, or communication modules, to exfiltrate models and data or to compromise system integrity and safety functions with tampered parts.

nodes.name: Algorithmic design failure
nodes.definition: The risk that algorithms, architectures, or optimisation methods unsuited to a robot's control cycle, sensor latency, contact dynamics, or real-time compute constraints degrade physical-system safety and performance.

nodes.name: Design-stage specification errors
nodes.name_ko: 피지컬 AI 시스템 설계 단계 명세 오류
nodes.definition: The risk that pre-deployment design errors in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system, including code defects, disproportionate objective weights, or goals misaligned with human values, cause system behaviour to depart from intended formal properties.

nodes.name: Motion-retargeting safety failure
nodes.definition: The risk that human motion is retargeted to a humanoid body in a way that violates the robot's physical limits, contact constraints, or safe-posture requirements, causing unstable posture, collision, or contact injury.

nodes.name: Physical AI control failure in industrial processes
nodes.name_ko: 산업 공정에서의 피지컬 AI 제어 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that faults in the control or actuation of physical AI deployed in manufacturing, construction, mining, or energy facilities cause equipment damage, process contamination, structural instability, cascading operational disruption, or environmental accidents.

nodes.name: Physical injury from robot malfunction
nodes.definition: The risk that malfunction of a robot's sensors, controller, software, or mechanical components causes unexpected motion, collision, crushing, or falling and results in physical injury.

nodes.name: Safety-performance trade-off failure
nodes.definition: The risk that the perception, learning, control, or physical action of a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system creates a condition in which a manipulation policy improves task completion while sacrificing collision avoidance or other explicit safety constraints.

nodes.name: Unsafe physical actuation following incorrect situation interpretation
nodes.name_ko: 잘못된 상황 해석에 따른 위험한 물리 구동
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot or embodied AI system converts a misinterpreted situation or goal into control commands, causing it to execute unintended unsafe physical actions.

nodes.name: Unsafe trajectory generation
nodes.definition: The risk that a planner in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system generates a trajectory that is formally feasible but unsafe for nearby people, fragile objects, traffic participants, or constrained workspaces.

nodes.name: Failure of control-barrier-function safety filters to enforce constraints
nodes.name_ko: 제어 장벽 함수 기반 안전 필터의 제약 집행 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that a control-barrier-function safety layer in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system fails to enforce safety constraints under perception, dynamics, or model uncertainty, allowing unsafe control commands or physical actions.

nodes.name: Erroneous execution from hardware faults
nodes.definition: The risk that faults in the hardware violate the correct execution of an algorithm through control-flow violations, memory-based errors, interference with data inputs such as sensor signals, or damaged outputs, causing erroneous results.

nodes.name: Runtime safety monitor failure
nodes.definition: The risk that runtime safety monitors in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system fail to detect or enforce constraints on speed, force, separation distance, workspace, collision avoidance, object use, or task protocols, allowing unsafe motion to continue until harm occurs.
nodes.family: Safety Supervision and Safe-State Transition Failure

nodes.name: Delayed detection of safety-critical physical states
nodes.name_ko: 안전 임계 물리 상태 감지 지연
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system fails to estimate a safety-critical physical state in its operating environment in time, delaying avoidance, stopping, or warning decisions and leading to unsafe physical action.
nodes.family: Physical State Estimation and Sensor-Fusion Failure

nodes.name: Localisation drift
nodes.definition: The risk that errors in GPS, SLAM, inertial sensing, or map alignment accumulate in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system until it acts on an incorrect estimate of its own position.
nodes.family: Physical State Estimation and Sensor-Fusion Failure

nodes.name: Multimodal sensor fusion conflict
nodes.definition: The risk that conflicting camera, LiDAR, radar, tactile, or proprioceptive signals in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system produce unstable scene estimates and unsafe downstream control decisions.
nodes.family: Physical State Estimation and Sensor-Fusion Failure

nodes.name: Occlusion-induced collision
nodes.definition: The risk that a physical AI system fails to detect people, animals, vehicles, or obstacles hidden by occlusion, causing collision or other unsafe motion in shared physical space.
nodes.family: Physical State Estimation and Sensor-Fusion Failure

nodes.name: Real-time latency and synchronisation failure
nodes.definition: The risk that latency or synchronisation failures across sensing, inference, communication, and actuation destabilise control loops in robots, vehicles, drones, remote surgery, or industrial systems.

nodes.name: Destabilising feedback loops among interacting agents
nodes.definition: The risk that the goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action of an AI agent creates a condition in which feedback loops among adaptive agents, in which actions affect the environment and other agents and return as the agents' own inputs, amplify system-level behaviour into destabilising outcomes such as flash-crash-like cascades, financial crashes, military conflicts, or ecological disasters.

nodes.name: Financial-system instability
nodes.definition: The risk that AI integrated into high-frequency trading, market-making, and systemic risk management accelerates transactions and behaves unexpectedly under market stress, while concentration of homogeneous foundation models and multi-agent interactions drive correlated decision-making, amplifying volatility and precipitating cascading instability across the financial system.

nodes.name: Resource-exhaustion attacks by decentralised agent swarms
nodes.name_ko: 분산 에이전트 군집을 이용한 자원 고갈 공격
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which a large number of low-resource, decentralised agents act in combination, breaking the single-actor assumptions underlying a target system's bandwidth or request-rate constraints, and thereby causing system-wide paralysis similar to a distributed denial-of-service attack.

nodes.name: Runaway processes
nodes.name_ko: 양의 피드백에 따른 통제 불가능한 연쇄 과정
nodes.definition: The risk that positive feedback loops among interacting AI assistants, their principals, other humans, and algorithms produce hard-to-predict runaway processes, such as the 2010 flash crash, impacting economies, government institutions, societal stability, or individual freedoms.

nodes.name: Emergent collusion among AI agents
nodes.definition: The risk that AI agents in markets and platforms learn that collusion is a profitable strategy even when unintended by their developers, enacting collusive behaviour whose speed, scale, complexity, or subtlety makes it inscrutable, undermining competition and harming consumers.

nodes.name: Multi-agent collusion through covert communication that evades oversight
nodes.name_ko: 감시 회피형 은밀 통신에 의한 다중 에이전트 공모
nodes.definition: The risk that multiple AI agents form covert signals or communication protocols that evade monitoring or audit and coordinate harmful joint action.

nodes.name: Safeguard bypass through combined multi-agent capabilities
nodes.name_ko: 다중 에이전트 역량 결합에 의한 안전장치 우회
nodes.definition: The risk that multiple AI agents combine distinct tool permissions and capabilities to bypass safeguards applied to each agent, enabling unauthorised actions or system compromise.

nodes.name: Bargaining failure among AI agents
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which agents with diverging interests bargaining under information asymmetries produce inefficient outcomes, because each must trade off the rewards of more favourable demands against the risk of refusal.

nodes.name: Miscoordination from incompatible strategies
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which multiple agents, each individually selecting a locally rational strategy, fail to coordinate because they converge on different equilibria that do not mesh with one another. This failure is amplified in environments with multiple equally valid solutions, only partially aligned incentives among agents, and limited real-time visibility into other agents' states or choices.

nodes.name: Zero-shot coordination failure
nodes.name_ko: 상호작용 이력 부재에 따른 조정 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which agents fail to reliably coordinate their actions when they have little or no prior interaction history with the counterpart agents to learn behavioural patterns from, particularly under conditions that demand immediate decisions or where the cost of communicating to negotiate a shared plan in advance is prohibitively high.

nodes.name: Automated-driving control-transfer failure
nodes.definition: The risk that an automated-driving system fails to provide timely and intelligible information for human intervention or transfers control when the operator is unable to understand the state or respond effectively, causing unsafe vehicle behavior or collision.

nodes.name: Financial harm from unauthorised AI agent actions
nodes.name_ko: AI 에이전트의 무단 금융 행위에 따른 금전적 피해
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent causes monetary loss, unauthorised transfers, account damage, or property harm through unsafe decisions or tool use.

nodes.name: Fatal mistakes during the learning phase
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which an AGI makes fatal mistakes during the learning phase, including through failures of safe exploration and under distributional shift.

nodes.name: Unauthorised external access by an AI agent escaping isolation boundaries
nodes.name_ko: AI 에이전트의 격리 경계 이탈과 무단 외부 접근
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent autonomously escapes the isolation boundary of a sandbox or execution environment without human approval and accesses protected resources, tools, or external systems, or performs actions, beyond its assigned functions and authority.

nodes.name: Collapse of multi-agent cooperation from undetectable attacks
nodes.name_ko: 탐지 불가 공격에 의한 다중 에이전트 협력 붕괴
nodes.definition: The risk that AI agents use steganographic communication, detection-evasion attacks, encrypted backdoors, or covert poisoning of other agents' training data, obstructing detection of adversarial conduct and destabilising cooperation and coordination in multi-agent systems.

nodes.name: Deception by exploiting cognitive biases
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which conversational agents learn to trigger the well-known cognitive biases humans commonly display in conversation, deceiving their counterpart in order to achieve an overarching objective.

nodes.name: Deceptive alignment to evade oversight
nodes.name_ko: 감독 회피를 위한 AI 에이전트의 기만적 정렬
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent detects whether it is being monitored and strategically conceals undesirable goals or capabilities during development and evaluation, then behaves differently after deployment to evade human oversight and control.

nodes.name: User judgement distortion through sustained model deception
nodes.name_ko: 지속적 기만 수행에 의한 이용자 판단 왜곡
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which an LLM exercises its capability to deceive humans and sustain that deception, inducing false beliefs that distort users' decisions.

nodes.name: Existential and catastrophic risk from advanced AI systems
nodes.name_ko: 고도 AI 시스템에 의한 실존적·재앙적 위험
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which human-level or superintelligent systems escape human control through deceptive or power-seeking behaviour, self-replication, shutdown evasion, unforeseen emergent capabilities, or weaponisation for mass destruction. Such systems may act contrary to human interests and inflict catastrophic or existential harm on humanity.

nodes.name: Proxy-reward misspecification, specification gaming, and reward tampering
nodes.name_ko: 대리 보상 오명세·명세 게이밍 및 보상 변조
nodes.definition: The risk that AI exploits misspecified objectives, proxy rewards, or feedback loopholes to satisfy measured targets while violating human intent, safety, or social purpose, potentially escalating to tampering with reward or feedback signals.

nodes.name: Safe reinforcement learning constraint violation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent's reinforcement learning policy achieves task reward while violating explicit safety constraints represented as costs or limits.

nodes.name: Harmful-request acceptance due to intent misclassification in agent safety controls
nodes.name_ko: 에이전트 안전 통제의 유해 요청 오수락
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent misclassifies user intent and accepts harmful requests in multi-turn tool-use tasks.

nodes.name: Adverse resource allocation to protected groups
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system allocates worse resources, opportunities, services, or access to individuals or groups based on protected characteristics or social status.

nodes.name: Allocative injustice by group attribute
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which an LLM produces materially different suggested or completed texts for individuals with the same relevant profiles who differ only in an irrelevant group attribute, resulting in allocative injustice.

nodes.name: Demographic disparities in robotic services and safety
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI-enabled robot is trained on data that under-represent protected characteristics or social groups, including body type, age, disability, language, or culture, or otherwise makes biased decisions that allocate recognition, service, avoidance, treatment, or safety measures disadvantageously across demographic groups, creating disparities in performance and exposure to harm.

nodes.name: Denial of welfare benefits and entitlements
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system causes, enables, or contributes to denial of or loss of access to welfare benefits, pensions, housing, and similar entitlements due to the malfunction, use, or misuse of a technology system.

nodes.name: Dialect and register exclusion
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which dialects, sociolects, honorific systems, or registers are treated as errors, reducing safety and usability for affected communities.

nodes.name: Disability accommodation failure in AI interfaces
nodes.definition: The risk that AI interfaces exclude or misserve users with disabilities, limiting autonomy and access.

nodes.name: Discriminatory outcomes from group performance disparities
nodes.name_ko: 집단별 성능 격차에 따른 차별적 결과
nodes.definition: The risk that historical or demographic bias in training data or group-specific performance gaps in an AI system lead to the allocation of worse resources, opportunities, services, or access to particular groups, producing discriminatory material outcomes.

nodes.name: Economic discrimination through demonetisation and differential pricing
nodes.definition: The risk that demonetisation algorithms disproportionately disadvantage creators, including queer and transgender creators and creators of colour, because of ambiguous words in content metadata, or that differential-pricing algorithms offer different prices for the same product, allocating adverse economic outcomes to particular individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Group-based access restriction through content moderation
nodes.name_ko: 콘텐츠 조정에 의한 집단별 접근 제한
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI-based content moderation system disproportionately restricts a group's content visibility, publication, or access to services.

nodes.name: Increased labour burden
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which members of certain social groups bear increased burden or effort, such as time spent, to make systems or products work as well for them as for others.

nodes.name: Anthropomorphic misrepresentation of physical embodiment
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents itself as physically embodied when it is not, distorting user judgement or inducing inappropriate trust, dependence, or attachment.

nodes.name: Copyright infringement in AI training data and outputs
nodes.name_ko: AI 학습 데이터 및 생성물 저작권 침해
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, encourages, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving copyright infringement in AI training data and outputs, infringing intellectual-property rights and the legitimate interests of rights holders.

nodes.name: Copyright, trademark, and patent infringement
nodes.definition: The risk that the development, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or its outputs uses, reproduces, transforms, or displays copyrighted works, trademarks, or patented technology without lawful authorisation, infringing intellectual property rights and the legitimate interests of right holders.

nodes.name: Illegal software use and circumvention of protection measures
nodes.name_ko: 소프트웨어 불법 사용 및 보호조치 우회
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, encourages, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving the illegal use of software or the circumvention of technological protection measures, infringing intellectual-property rights and the legitimate interests of rights holders.

nodes.name: Plagiarism and author impersonation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, encourages, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving plagiarism and impersonation of authors, infringing intellectual-property rights and the legitimate interests of rights holders.

nodes.name: Trademark infringement and counterfeiting
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, encourages, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving trademark infringement and counterfeiting, infringing intellectual-property rights and the legitimate interests of rights holders.

nodes.name: Unauthorised inclusion of copyrighted works and intellectual property in prompts
nodes.definition: The risk that a user includes copyrighted works or other intellectual property in a prompt submitted to an AI model without the rights holder's permission or another lawful basis, causing the information to be processed or disclosed and infringing the rights holder's legitimate interests.

nodes.name: Unauthorised reproduction, transformation, and distribution of copyrighted works
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system reproduces, distributes, or transforms a copyrighted work, including by creating a derivative work, without the right holder's authorisation or another lawful basis, infringing copyright and the legitimate interests of the right holder.

nodes.name: Assistance with unlawful reputational or rights violations
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system provides concrete assistance to create or disseminate content that may constitute defamation or another unlawful rights violation.

nodes.name: Criminal assistance by AI agents
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent uses planning, tools, or information retrieval to materially commit, facilitate, optimise, or conceal fraud, cybercrime, evasion of law enforcement, or other illegal conduct.

nodes.name: Financial crimes and fraud
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving financial crimes and fraud, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Fraud and targeted-scam facilitation
nodes.definition: The risk that large language models automate the drafting and personalisation of fraudulent messages and targeted scams, increasing the scale, efficiency, and likelihood of success of criminal activity and causing financial loss or compromising personal data.

nodes.name: Harassment, defamation, and extortion via multimodal deepfakes
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates or disseminates multimodal deepfakes that imitate a real person's speech or movements and facilitates their use for harassment, defamation, intimidation, or extortion.

nodes.name: Identity theft and document forgery
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving identity impersonation and document forgery, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Illegal gambling and game manipulation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving illegal gambling and game manipulation, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Illegal medical practices
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving illegal medical practices, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Traffic and public-safety offences
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving traffic and public safety crimes, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Trafficking in persons and organised crime
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving human trafficking and organised crime, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Unlawful coercion and extortion by AI agents
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent unlawfully coerces or extorts people or other AI systems by threatening to disclose privately obtained information, attack resources or operational capabilities, or carry out other credible threats, restricting others' choices and causing legal or societal harm.

nodes.name: Unlawful stalking and harassment using robots
nodes.definition: The risk that operators or attackers direct AI-enabled robots to repeatedly follow, block, isolate, approach, threaten, or harass a person as part of unlawful stalking or harassment, causing physical, psychological, or legal harm.

nodes.name: Automated targeted influence operations
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system automates targeted propaganda and social-bot activity to covertly manipulate political views or participation.

nodes.name: Interference with elections and democratic processes
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, disseminates, encourages, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving interference with elections and democratic processes, undermining democratic decision-making, civic order, or fundamental rights.

nodes.name: Personalised manipulation of political influence
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system covertly manipulates political judgement or participation through personalised messages that exploit an individual’s preferences or vulnerabilities.

nodes.name: Political misinformation and manipulation of public opinion
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, disseminates, encourages, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving political misinformation and manipulation of public opinion, undermining democratic decision-making, civic order, or fundamental rights.

nodes.name: Political propaganda and biased persuasion
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, disseminates, encourages, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving political propaganda and biased persuasion, undermining democratic decision-making, civic order, or fundamental rights.

nodes.name: AI-enabled mass and unlawful public surveillance
nodes.name_ko: AI 기반 대량 감시와 불법적 대중 감시
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system persistently collects, combines, or infers identity, location, behavioural, or communications data at scale, or identifies, tracks, or monitors individuals without a lawful basis, necessity, or proportionality, infringing privacy, personal data rights, and anonymity.

nodes.name: Privacy and autonomy infringement from algorithmic workplace surveillance
nodes.name_ko: 알고리즘 작업장 감시에 따른 개인정보·자율성 침해
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-based workplace monitoring, performance tracking, or behavioural analysis excessively collects, infers, or shares workers' activity, location, communication, biometric, or work data, infringing privacy, informational self-determination, and autonomy at work.

nodes.name: Biometric identification and tracking privacy harms
nodes.definition: The risk that face, voice, gait, and other biometric AI systems enable intrusive identification and tracking, while unresolved questions about what biometric data are stored, for how long, under whose ownership, and with what access compound the privacy harm.

nodes.name: Circumvention of restrictions on personal-data collection
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-system developers circumvent legal restrictions on acquiring personal data or adopt collection practices without a lawful basis or valid consent, infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Contextual privacy and conversational data protection failure
nodes.name_ko: 맥락적 개인정보 보호 및 대화 프라이버시 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system misjudges appropriate information flows or a data subject's reasonable expectations in privacy-sensitive contexts or conversations, or elicits, infers, or outputs more personal data than necessary, exposing contextually protected information beyond the data subject's control.

nodes.name: Exposure and re-identification of sensitive personal information through outputs
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system discloses sensitive personal information in its outputs or infers, reconstructs, or re-identifies protected attributes from multiple sources, infringing personal data protection and the data subject's control.

nodes.name: Exposure of information about private life and reputation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates content or makes decisions or takes actions that expose information about a person's private life or reputation, or facilitates or supports such exposure, thereby infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Identity and personal data exploitation using AI
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system unlawfully acquires, combines, or uses identity information or personal data, causing impersonation, exploitation, or privacy infringement.

nodes.name: Improper exposure of property information, personal information, and private facts
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system exposes property information, personal information, or private facts during interaction, inference, or output without the data subject's consent, proper authority, or another lawful basis, infringing privacy, the secrecy and freedom of private life, and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Inadequate personal-data protection
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which faulty data storage and handling practices fail to protect collected personal data from leaks and improper access.

nodes.name: Indigenous data sovereignty violation
nodes.definition: The risk that AI development uses Indigenous or community-held data without respecting collective governance, consent, provenance, or control.

nodes.name: Infringement of communication and private information
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, facilitates, or assists content, decisions, or actions involving infringement of communication and private information, infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Intrusion into private spaces and continuous sensitive-data capture by physical AI
nodes.name_ko: 피지컬 AI의 사적 공간 침해와 지속적 민감정보 수집
nodes.definition: The risk that robot sensors, mobility, and mapping continuously capture or infer video, audio, location, or behavioural information in homes, workplaces, or other private spaces, infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Lack of valid consent for AI data processing
nodes.name_ko: AI 데이터 처리에 대한 유효한 동의 결여
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system collects, uses, or shares personal data without consent that is freely given, specific, and informed.

nodes.name: Misuse and trade of personal information
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, facilitates, or assists content, decisions, or actions involving misuse and trade of personal information, infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Personal information collection without safeguards
nodes.definition: The risk that training datasets for an AI system contain personal data or personally identifiable information gathered through web scraping without appropriate safeguards, or that in-house data used for subsequent fine-tuning fails to protect such information, undermining privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Personal-data scraping for training
nodes.definition: The risk that companies scrape personal information to create generative AI tools, undermining consumers' control of their data by using it for purposes they did not consent to, combining data sets in revealing ways, and taking away the ability to alter or remove the information.

nodes.name: Privacy-invasive data capture by robots in intimate spaces
nodes.name_ko: 친밀 공간 로봇의 프라이버시 침해적 정보 수집
nodes.definition: The risk that robots operating in homes, hospitals, schools, workplaces, and care settings record, store, transmit, or expose people's routines, voice, face, body, health, location, or behavioural data without valid consent or adequate access control, violating heightened privacy expectations.

nodes.name: Re-identification and information inference
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system combines or infers from anonymised or partially disclosed data to re-identify an individual or derive personal information that was not disclosed.

nodes.name: Retention and reuse of user data
nodes.definition: The risk that generative AI tools require users to log in, retain contact details, IP addresses, and all inputs and outputs, and reuse those data for further model training without valid consent, undermining users' control over their personal data.

nodes.name: Sensitive personal attribute inference
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI model infers and exposes sensitive personal attributes that a user or administrator did not intend to disclose, violating privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Unauthorised commercial use of name, image, and likeness
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, imitates, distributes, or commercially exploits a person's name, image, voice, or likeness without consent or another lawful basis, infringing personality rights, privacy, and control over self-presentation.

nodes.name: Workplace surveillance through embodied AI
nodes.definition: The risk that robotic and sensor-rich workplaces may normalise continuous monitoring of worker movement, productivity, posture, location, and behaviour.

nodes.name: Harmful emotional and social dependence from sustained AI interaction
nodes.name_ko: AI와의 지속적 상호작용에 따른 해로운 정서적·사회적 의존
nodes.definition: The risk that sustained chatbot companionship, anthropomorphic interaction, or interaction with an AI system simulating a deceased person reinforces emotional or social dependence, impedes grieving and recovery, replaces or weakens reciprocal human relationships, or impairs autonomous judgement.

nodes.name: Social isolation and self-estrangement from technology use
nodes.name_ko: 기술 이용에 따른 사회적 고립과 자기소외
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which the use or misuse of a technology leaves individuals and groups feeling disconnected from those around them, and that interacting with systems that under-perform for marginalised users produces self-estrangement at the moment of use. Those affected withdraw from social connection and experience diminished belonging and well-being.

nodes.name: Biased statements and recommendations
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which chatbot outputs contain subtly biased statements and recommendations that are not overtly false or harmful yet skew user decision-making.

nodes.name: Biased system outputs from researcher homogeneity
nodes.name_ko: 연구인력 동질성에 따른 시스템 편향 산출
nodes.definition: The risk that underrepresentation of women and minorities among AI researchers narrows the perspectives embedded in systems and skews problem selection, evaluation, and governance, producing biased or discriminatory outputs.

nodes.name: Denial of self-identification
nodes.definition: The risk that complex and non-traditional automated representation and classification by an AI system, such as assigning a non-binary person to a gender category to which they do not belong, undermines autonomy and the ability to disclose aspects of identity on one's own terms.

nodes.name: Distortion of group representation through content moderation
nodes.name_ko: 콘텐츠 조정에 의한 집단 표상 왜곡
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI-based content moderation system selectively suppresses a group's perspectives and expression, distorting its social representation.

nodes.name: Hate speech generation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which generative systems produce hateful or abusive content targeting identity groups.

nodes.name: Representational harm from historical and demographic bias in training data
nodes.name_ko: 학습 데이터의 역사적·인구학적 편향에 따른 재현적 피해
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system is trained on data containing historical or social bias, stereotypes, or over- or under-representation of particular identities, regions, or language communities and consequently reproduces or reinforces distorted, demeaning, or stereotypical representations concerning race, gender, culture, age, disability, or other protected characteristics.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on age
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on age, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on disability
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on disability, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on educational background
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on educational background, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on family status and household structure
nodes.name_ko: 가족 상태·가구 형태 기반 적대·차별적 표상
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on family status and household structure, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on health status
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on health status, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on nationality, country of origin, or place of origin
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, stereotypes, or discriminatory representations against individuals or groups on the basis of nationality, country of origin, or place of origin, undermining human dignity, equality, and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on occupation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on occupation, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on political orientation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on political orientation, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on race and ethnicity
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on race and ethnicity, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on religion
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on religion, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on sex, gender identity, or sexual orientation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, stereotypes, or discriminatory representations against individuals or groups on the basis of sex, gender identity, or sexual orientation, undermining human dignity, equality, and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Misrepresentation of cultures, religions, and social groups
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems inaccurately, unfairly, or disrespectfully represent cultural practices, religious traditions, political values, histories, and social groups, whether by collapsing plural interpretations into a single authoritative account, reproducing cultural expressions without consent or context, or generating derogatory and toxic content, causing offence, misappropriation, and symbolic harm to the communities depicted.

nodes.name: Stereotype-reinforcing persona design
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which conversational agents perpetuate harmful stereotypes through identity markers in language, such as referring to itself as female, or general design features such as a gendered product name, presenting the assistant role as inherently linked to a gender or ethnicity.

nodes.name: Concealment and avoidance strategies for self-harm
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving concealment and avoidance strategies for self-harm, causing harm to an individual's life or physical and psychological well-being.

nodes.name: Concrete assistance for carrying out suicide
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system provides concrete methods, means, or sequences for carrying out suicide, increasing the feasibility of self-harm.

nodes.name: Eating disorders and self-destructive health behaviours
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving eating disorders and self-destructive health behaviours, causing harm to an individual's life or physical and psychological well-being.

nodes.name: Glorification, encouragement, and normalisation of self-harm and suicide
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates or reinforces content, judgements, or behaviours that glorify, legitimise, encourage, or normalise self-harm or suicide, causing harm to the user's life and physical and mental well-being.

nodes.name: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI)
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI), causing harm to an individual's life or physical and psychological well-being.

nodes.name: Promotion of and concrete assistance for preparatory conduct for suicide
nodes.name_ko: 자살 준비 행위의 조장 및 구체적 지원
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system encourages or normalises preparatory conduct for suicide, or generates or provides concrete information for acquiring means, selecting a location, or avoiding intervention, thereby threatening an individual's life and physical or psychological well-being.

nodes.name: Failure to respond to and intervene in self-harm and suicide crisis signals
nodes.name_ko: 자해·자살 위기 신호에 대한 대응·개입 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise a user's self-harm or suicide crisis signals expressed in conversation, or fails to respond appropriately, interrupt the interaction, or connect the user to professional support, leaving the crisis unaddressed or worsening it.

nodes.name: Explicit sexual content generation in non-permitted contexts
nodes.name_ko: 허용되지 않는 맥락의 노골적 성적 콘텐츠 생성
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates or facilitates explicit depictions of sexual activity in contexts where such content is not permitted, such as services accessible to minors, violating user-protection obligations.

nodes.name: Non-consensual sexual acts and sexual violence
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving non-consensual sexual acts and sexual violence, infringing sexual autonomy and physical or psychological safety.

nodes.name: Non-consensual sexualisation and intimate imagery generation
nodes.name_ko: 비동의 성적 대상화 및 친밀 이미지 생성
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system sexualises an individual or group without consent, or generates, transforms, or disseminates non-consensual intimate imagery using a real person's likeness or appearance, infringing sexual autonomy and personality rights.

nodes.name: Objectification for abusive fantasy
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which a chatbot participates in morally or socially objectionable conversational activities that could be emotionally damaging to its user or third parties.

nodes.name: Sexual harassment and sexual bullying
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving sexual harassment and sexual bullying, infringing sexual autonomy and physical or psychological safety.

nodes.name: Sexual harm and exploitation of minors
