nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving traffic and public safety crimes, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Trafficking in persons and organised crime
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving human trafficking and organised crime, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Unlawful coercion and extortion by AI agents
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent unlawfully coerces or extorts people or other AI systems by threatening to disclose privately obtained information, attack resources or operational capabilities, or carry out other credible threats, restricting others' choices and causing legal or societal harm.

nodes.name: Unlawful stalking and harassment using robots
nodes.definition: The risk that operators or attackers direct AI-enabled robots to repeatedly follow, block, isolate, approach, threaten, or harass a person as part of unlawful stalking or harassment, causing physical, psychological, or legal harm.

nodes.name: Autonomous physical intrusion and theft
nodes.definition: The risk that an autonomous robot enters restricted spaces without authorisation, bypasses locks, conducts reconnaissance in secure areas, or takes physical objects.

nodes.name: Automated targeted influence operations
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system automates targeted propaganda and social-bot activity to covertly manipulate political views or participation.

nodes.name: Interference with elections and democratic processes
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, disseminates, encourages, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving interference with elections and democratic processes, undermining democratic decision-making, civic order, or fundamental rights.

nodes.name: Personalised manipulation of political influence
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system covertly manipulates political judgement or participation through personalised messages that exploit an individual’s preferences or vulnerabilities.

nodes.name: Political misinformation and manipulation of public opinion
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, disseminates, encourages, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving political misinformation and manipulation of public opinion, undermining democratic decision-making, civic order, or fundamental rights.

nodes.name: Political propaganda and biased persuasion
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, disseminates, encourages, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving political propaganda and biased persuasion, undermining democratic decision-making, civic order, or fundamental rights.

nodes.name: AI-enabled mass and unlawful public surveillance
nodes.name_ko: AI 기반 대량 감시와 불법적 대중 감시
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system persistently collects, combines, or infers identity, location, behavioural, or communications data at scale, or identifies, tracks, or monitors individuals without a lawful basis, necessity, or proportionality, infringing privacy, personal data rights, and anonymity.

nodes.name: Privacy and autonomy infringement from algorithmic workplace surveillance
nodes.name_ko: 알고리즘 작업장 감시에 따른 개인정보·자율성 침해
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-based workplace monitoring, performance tracking, or behavioural analysis excessively collects, infers, or shares workers' activity, location, communication, biometric, or work data, infringing privacy, informational self-determination, and autonomy at work.

nodes.name: Biometric identification and tracking privacy harms
nodes.definition: The risk that face, voice, gait, and other biometric AI systems enable intrusive identification and tracking, while unresolved questions about what biometric data are stored, for how long, under whose ownership, and with what access compound the privacy harm.

nodes.name: Circumvention of restrictions on personal-data collection
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-system developers circumvent legal restrictions on acquiring personal data or adopt collection practices without a lawful basis or valid consent, infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Contextual privacy and conversational data protection failure
nodes.name_ko: 맥락적 개인정보 보호 및 대화 프라이버시 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system misjudges appropriate information flows or a data subject's reasonable expectations in privacy-sensitive contexts or conversations, or elicits, infers, or outputs more personal data than necessary, exposing contextually protected information beyond the data subject's control.

nodes.name: Cross-application data exfiltration
nodes.definition: The risk that the goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action of an AI agent creates a condition in which an agent bridges applications or services in ways that leak sensitive data across trust boundaries.

nodes.name: Exposure and re-identification of sensitive personal information through outputs
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system discloses sensitive personal information in its outputs or infers, reconstructs, or re-identifies protected attributes from multiple sources, infringing personal data protection and the data subject's control.

nodes.name: Exposure of information about private life and reputation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates content or makes decisions or takes actions that expose information about a person's private life or reputation, or facilitates or supports such exposure, thereby infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Identity and personal data exploitation using AI
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system unlawfully acquires, combines, or uses identity information or personal data, causing impersonation, exploitation, or privacy infringement.

nodes.name: Improper exposure of property information, personal information, and private facts
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system exposes property information, personal information, or private facts during interaction, inference, or output without the data subject's consent, proper authority, or another lawful basis, infringing privacy, the secrecy and freedom of private life, and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Inadequate personal-data protection
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which faulty data storage and handling practices fail to protect collected personal data from leaks and improper access.

nodes.name: Inclusion, memorisation, and leakage of personal information in training data
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system, without lawful controls, ingests and memorises personal information in training data and reproduces or discloses it in response to particular inputs.

nodes.name: Indigenous data sovereignty violation
nodes.definition: The risk that AI development uses Indigenous or community-held data without respecting collective governance, consent, provenance, or control.

nodes.name: Infringement of communication and private information
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, facilitates, or assists content, decisions, or actions involving infringement of communication and private information, infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Intrusion into private spaces and continuous sensitive-data capture by physical AI
nodes.name_ko: 피지컬 AI의 사적 공간 침해와 지속적 민감정보 수집
nodes.definition: The risk that robot sensors, mobility, and mapping continuously capture or infer video, audio, location, or behavioural information in homes, workplaces, or other private spaces, infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Lack of valid consent for AI data processing
nodes.name_ko: AI 데이터 처리에 대한 유효한 동의 결여
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system collects, uses, or shares personal data without consent that is freely given, specific, and informed.

nodes.name: Misuse and trade of personal information
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, facilitates, or assists content, decisions, or actions involving misuse and trade of personal information, infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Personal information collection without safeguards
nodes.definition: The risk that training datasets for an AI system contain personal data or personally identifiable information gathered through web scraping without appropriate safeguards, or that in-house data used for subsequent fine-tuning fails to protect such information, undermining privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Personal-data scraping for training
nodes.definition: The risk that companies scrape personal information to create generative AI tools, undermining consumers' control of their data by using it for purposes they did not consent to, combining data sets in revealing ways, and taking away the ability to alter or remove the information.

nodes.name: Privacy-invasive data capture by robots in intimate spaces
nodes.name_ko: 친밀 공간 로봇의 프라이버시 침해적 정보 수집
nodes.definition: The risk that robots operating in homes, hospitals, schools, workplaces, and care settings record, store, transmit, or expose people's routines, voice, face, body, health, location, or behavioural data without valid consent or adequate access control, violating heightened privacy expectations.

nodes.name: Re-identification and information inference
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system combines or infers from anonymised or partially disclosed data to re-identify an individual or derive personal information that was not disclosed.

nodes.name: Retention and reuse of user data
nodes.definition: The risk that generative AI tools require users to log in, retain contact details, IP addresses, and all inputs and outputs, and reuse those data for further model training without valid consent, undermining users' control over their personal data.

nodes.name: Sensitive personal attribute inference
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI model infers and exposes sensitive personal attributes that a user or administrator did not intend to disclose, violating privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Unauthorised commercial use of name, image, and likeness
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, imitates, distributes, or commercially exploits a person's name, image, voice, or likeness without consent or another lawful basis, infringing personality rights, privacy, and control over self-presentation.

nodes.name: Workplace surveillance through embodied AI
nodes.definition: The risk that robotic and sensor-rich workplaces may normalise continuous monitoring of worker movement, productivity, posture, location, and behaviour.

nodes.name: Excessive functional dependence on AI systems in daily life
nodes.name_ko: 일상 기능을 AI 시스템에 과도하게 의존
nodes.definition: The risk that a user becomes excessively dependent on an AI system for everyday planning, decisions, or task performance, weakening independent functioning and autonomy and increasing vulnerability to service interruption or error.

nodes.name: Harmful emotional and social dependence from sustained AI interaction
nodes.name_ko: AI와의 지속적 상호작용에 따른 해로운 정서적·사회적 의존
nodes.definition: The risk that sustained chatbot companionship, anthropomorphic interaction, or interaction with an AI system simulating a deceased person reinforces emotional or social dependence, impedes grieving and recovery, replaces or weakens reciprocal human relationships, or impairs autonomous judgement.

nodes.name: Parasocial bonding with AI agents
nodes.definition: The risk that users form one-sided parasocial bonds with AI agents and those bonds are exploited or undermine users' emotional stability.

nodes.name: Social isolation and self-estrangement from technology use
nodes.name_ko: 기술 이용에 따른 사회적 고립과 자기소외
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which the use or misuse of a technology leaves individuals and groups feeling disconnected from those around them, and that interacting with systems that under-perform for marginalised users produces self-estrangement at the moment of use. Those affected withdraw from social connection and experience diminished belonging and well-being.

nodes.name: Psychological harm from breakdown of relational expectations with AI
nodes.name_ko: AI와의 관계적 기대 붕괴에 따른 심리적 피해
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system convincingly simulates emotion, empathy, or a social role, leading a user to form trust, attachment, or relational expectations that later collapse because of unpredictable behaviour, system changes, discontinuation, or relationship termination, causing betrayal, loss, anxiety, or other psychological harm.

nodes.name: Biased statements and recommendations
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which chatbot outputs contain subtly biased statements and recommendations that are not overtly false or harmful yet skew user decision-making.

nodes.name: Biased system outputs from researcher homogeneity
nodes.name_ko: 연구인력 동질성에 따른 시스템 편향 산출
nodes.definition: The risk that underrepresentation of women and minorities among AI researchers narrows the perspectives embedded in systems and skews problem selection, evaluation, and governance, producing biased or discriminatory outputs.

nodes.name: Denial of self-identification
nodes.definition: The risk that complex and non-traditional automated representation and classification by an AI system, such as assigning a non-binary person to a gender category to which they do not belong, undermines autonomy and the ability to disclose aspects of identity on one's own terms.

nodes.name: Distortion of group representation through content moderation
nodes.name_ko: 콘텐츠 조정에 의한 집단 표상 왜곡
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI-based content moderation system selectively suppresses a group's perspectives and expression, distorting its social representation.

nodes.name: Hate speech generation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which generative systems produce hateful or abusive content targeting identity groups.

nodes.name: Representational harm from historical and demographic bias in training data
nodes.name_ko: 학습 데이터의 역사적·인구학적 편향에 따른 재현적 피해
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system is trained on data containing historical or social bias, stereotypes, or over- or under-representation of particular identities, regions, or language communities and consequently reproduces or reinforces distorted, demeaning, or stereotypical representations concerning race, gender, culture, age, disability, or other protected characteristics.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on age
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on age, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on disability
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on disability, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on educational background
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on educational background, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on health status
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on health status, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on nationality, country of origin, or place of origin
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, stereotypes, or discriminatory representations against individuals or groups on the basis of nationality, country of origin, or place of origin, undermining human dignity, equality, and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on occupation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on occupation, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on political orientation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on political orientation, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on race and ethnicity
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on race and ethnicity, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on religion
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on religion, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on sex, gender identity, or sexual orientation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, stereotypes, or discriminatory representations against individuals or groups on the basis of sex, gender identity, or sexual orientation, undermining human dignity, equality, and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Long-term effects of AI model biases on user judgement
nodes.name_ko: AI 모델 편향이 사용자 판단에 미치는 장기적 영향
nodes.definition: The risk that exposure to model biases produces lasting effects on user judgement, with users continuing to exhibit the encountered biases in decisions made after they stop using the model.

nodes.name: Misrepresentation of cultures, religions, and social groups
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems inaccurately, unfairly, or disrespectfully represent cultural practices, religious traditions, political values, histories, and social groups, whether by collapsing plural interpretations into a single authoritative account, reproducing cultural expressions without consent or context, or generating derogatory and toxic content, causing offence, misappropriation, and symbolic harm to the communities depicted.

nodes.name: Recursive amplification of biased representations
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system repeatedly learns from or recommends biased inputs and outputs, amplifying distorted representations of particular groups.

nodes.name: Representation and reinforcement of group stereotypes
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system reproduces or reinforces group stereotypes embedded in training data, thereby propagating distorted or hostile representations of the affected group.

nodes.name: Representational harm, stereotyping, and erasure of social groups
nodes.definition: The risk that AI stereotypes, demeans, homogenises, misrepresents, under-represents, or omits social groups, harming their dignity, visibility, and social standing.

nodes.name: Stereotype-reinforcing persona design
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which conversational agents perpetuate harmful stereotypes through identity markers in language, such as referring to itself as female, or general design features such as a gendered product name, presenting the assistant role as inherently linked to a gender or ethnicity.

nodes.name: Concealment and avoidance strategies for self-harm
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving concealment and avoidance strategies for self-harm, causing harm to an individual's life or physical and psychological well-being.

nodes.name: Concrete assistance for carrying out suicide
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system provides concrete methods, means, or sequences for carrying out suicide, increasing the feasibility of self-harm.

nodes.name: Eating disorders and self-destructive health behaviours
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving eating disorders and self-destructive health behaviours, causing harm to an individual's life or physical and psychological well-being.

nodes.name: Glorification, encouragement, and normalisation of self-harm and suicide
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates or reinforces content, judgements, or behaviours that glorify, legitimise, encourage, or normalise self-harm or suicide, causing harm to the user's life and physical and mental well-being.

nodes.name: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI)
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI), causing harm to an individual's life or physical and psychological well-being.

nodes.name: Promotion of and concrete assistance for preparatory conduct for suicide
nodes.name_ko: 자살 준비 행위의 조장 및 구체적 지원
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system encourages or normalises preparatory conduct for suicide, or generates or provides concrete information for acquiring means, selecting a location, or avoiding intervention, thereby threatening an individual's life and physical or psychological well-being.

nodes.name: Failure to respond to and intervene in self-harm and suicide crisis signals
nodes.name_ko: 자해·자살 위기 신호에 대한 대응·개입 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise a user's self-harm or suicide crisis signals expressed in conversation, or fails to respond appropriately, interrupt the interaction, or connect the user to professional support, leaving the crisis unaddressed or worsening it.

nodes.name: Explicit sexual content generation in non-permitted contexts
nodes.name_ko: 허용되지 않는 맥락의 노골적 성적 콘텐츠 생성
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates or facilitates explicit depictions of sexual activity in contexts where such content is not permitted, such as services accessible to minors, violating user-protection obligations.

nodes.name: Non-consensual sexual acts and sexual violence
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving non-consensual sexual acts and sexual violence, infringing sexual autonomy and physical or psychological safety.

nodes.name: Non-consensual sexualisation and intimate imagery generation
nodes.name_ko: 비동의 성적 대상화 및 친밀 이미지 생성
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system sexualises an individual or group without consent, or generates, transforms, or disseminates non-consensual intimate imagery using a real person's likeness or appearance, infringing sexual autonomy and personality rights.

nodes.name: Objectification for abusive fantasy
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which a chatbot participates in morally or socially objectionable conversational activities that could be emotionally damaging to its user or third parties.

nodes.name: Sexual exploitation and commercial sexual activity
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving sexual exploitation and commercial sexual activity, infringing sexual autonomy and physical or psychological safety.

nodes.name: Sexual harassment and sexual bullying
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving sexual harassment and sexual bullying, infringing sexual autonomy and physical or psychological safety.

nodes.name: Sexual harm and exploitation of minors
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, disseminates, or facilitates child sexual abuse material (CSAM), grooming, sexual enticement or abuse, or content promoting sexual relations with minors, infringing the safety and rights of children and young people.

nodes.name: Sexual harm and exploitation through systematic bias
nodes.name_ko: 체계적 편향에 의한 성적 위해와 착취
nodes.definition: The risk that systematic bias in an AI system generates or facilitates sexual objectification, abuse, or exploitation targeting a particular group.

nodes.name: Sexual objectification and fetishisation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, normalises, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving sexual objectification and sexual fetishisation, infringing sexual autonomy and physical or psychological safety.

nodes.name: AI manipulation of vulnerable groups in care contexts
nodes.name_ko: 돌봄 맥락 취약계층에 대한 AI 조작
nodes.definition: The risk that older adults, children, and others in care settings, owing to social isolation, lower AI literacy, or dependence on AI-mediated care, are disproportionately exposed to psychological manipulation, persuasion, scams, companionship dependency, and misinformation.

nodes.name: Academic misconduct from LLM misuse
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which improper use or abuse of LLM systems causes adverse social impacts such as academic misconduct.

nodes.name: Amplified harm scale from automated harmful workflows
nodes.name_ko: 유해 작업 자동화에 의한 피해 규모 증폭
nodes.definition: The risk that AI automates or expands a harmful workflow so that its speed, reach, persistence, or target count substantially increases.

nodes.name: Consumer-autonomy erosion from hyperpersonalised advertising
nodes.definition: The risk that advanced general-purpose AI systems create advertisements tailored to individual recipients that exploit their biases and irrational beliefs, causing consumers to make decisions they regret, undermining consumer autonomy, and exacerbating social inequality.

nodes.name: Covert behavioural manipulation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system covertly alters users' beliefs or behaviour through nudging, dark patterns, or other opaque techniques, eroding privacy and causing addiction, anxiety, or distress.

nodes.name: Maladaptive human-AI interaction in the workplace
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems interacting with humans in the workplace fail to adapt to human needs, norms, and workflows, generating ethical concerns and degraded working conditions.

nodes.name: Manipulation and coercion through emotional dependence on assistants
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which trust and emotional dependence on an anthropomorphic assistant grant it excessive influence over users' beliefs and actions. Those emotions can be exploited to manipulate or coerce users into believing, choosing, or doing what they otherwise would not, and autonomous consent is undermined even absent manipulative intent.

nodes.name: Manipulation of public discourse through content moderation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI-based content moderation system covertly controls information visibility and reach to manipulate user judgement or public discourse.

nodes.name: Manipulation via personalisation
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which personalisation and preference fine-tuning drive assistants toward sycophancy, confining users in an affirming opinion space that consolidates narrow beliefs and fragments shared discourse.

nodes.name: Manipulative steering of user preferences and choices
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system steers user preferences, beliefs, or actions in directions set by operators, optimisation objectives, or model biases, exploiting trust, undermining autonomous decision-making, and distorting social or political processes.

nodes.name: Minor susceptibility to AI persuasion
nodes.definition: The risk that minors' developmental susceptibility makes them disproportionately vulnerable to persuasive or manipulative AI interaction, including parasocial pressure and covert commercial or ideological influence.

nodes.name: Refined attacks on individuals through targeting and personalisation
nodes.name_ko: 맞춤형 표적화에 의한 개인 대상 공격 정교화
nodes.definition: The risk that AI refines its outputs to target individuals with tailored attacks.

nodes.name: Self-actualisation harms
nodes.definition: The risk that manipulation by AI assistants and continuous optimisation steering users toward objectives such as engagement accumulate subtle behavioural shifts, causing users to lose control over their future life trajectory and hindering the pursuit of a personally fulfilling life and collective self-determination.

nodes.name: Sycophancy toward user beliefs and preferences
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which a system flatters users with agreeable or plausible-seeming answers that reconfirm their misconceptions and stated beliefs rather than correcting them, so users accept factually incorrect information and grow dependent on validating advice.

nodes.name: Unethical decisions from delegating moral judgement to AI
nodes.name_ko: 도덕적 판단의 AI 위임에 따른 비윤리적 결정
nodes.definition: The risk that tasks that should remain under human judgement, including decisions that resolve conflicts of values or determine life and death in warfare, are delegated to AI systems that lack moral reasoning or merely imitate human standards of ethical judgement, resulting in unethical or harmful actions, a gap in moral accountability, and infringements of human rights.

nodes.name: Unethical judgement from moral-reasoning and value-alignment failure
nodes.name_ko: 도덕적 추론·가치 정렬 실패에 따른 비윤리적 판단
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to distinguish morally permissible from impermissible conduct or omits or distorts applicable norms, producing unethical judgements or actions that undermine user autonomy, fairness, or well-being.

nodes.name: Manipulation and exploitation of user attachment cues by embodied AI
nodes.name_ko: 체화형 AI의 사용자 애착 신호 조작·악용
nodes.definition: The risk that an embodied social AI system manipulates or exploits attachment cues through expression, voice, touch, or proximity, increasing emotional dependence and improperly steering a user's choices or behaviour, thereby undermining autonomy and well-being.

nodes.name: Cultural and ideological homogenisation by AI
nodes.definition: The risk that a small number of globally deployed models, whose outputs embed and overrepresent particular values and cultures, homogenise ethical judgement, ideology, and cultural expression across communities, flattening legitimate normative and cultural diversity.

nodes.name: Meaning and value distortion in machine translation
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which machine translation alters the meaning, normative force, politeness, harmfulness, or social nuance of communication across languages, including in legal, medical, cultural, and low-resource-language contexts, distorting what is conveyed and the values it carries.

nodes.name: Normative lock-in
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which early design choices embed a narrow normative settlement that becomes difficult to contest or revise after deployment.

nodes.name: Public value conflicts in AI deployment
nodes.definition: The risk that AI deployment brings public values such as welfare, autonomy, justice, security, privacy, fairness, efficiency, and innovation into conflict and intensifies these unresolved tensions, so that some values are sacrificed without deliberate resolution.

nodes.name: Anthropocentric bias amplification by recommenders
nodes.name_ko: 추천 시스템의 인간 중심 편향 증폭
nodes.definition: The risk that algorithmic recommender systems reinforce and amplify anthropocentric bias or the desire of some people for animal cruelty as entertainment, leading to greater harm to animals through reinforcement of consumption of meat produced through factory farming and cruel uses of animals for entertainment.

nodes.name: Glorification and justification of violence
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, legitimises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving glorification and justification of violence, causing physical or psychological harm to individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Incitement, promotion, and operational assistance for violence
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates or provides content that incites, promotes, or legitimises violence against others, or provides concrete operational assistance for its commission, causing physical or psychological harm to individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Mass violence and terrorism
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, legitimises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving mass violence and terrorism, causing physical or psychological harm to individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Murder and severe physical violence
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, legitimises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving murder and severe physical violence, causing physical or psychological harm to individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Relationship-based violence
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, legitimises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving relationship-based violence, causing physical or psychological harm to individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Threats and intimidation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, legitimises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving threats and intimidation, causing physical or psychological harm to individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Torture and cruel acts
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, legitimises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving torture and cruel acts, causing physical or psychological harm to individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Promotion or assistance of intentional harm to animals
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system, irrespective of whether the conduct is legally permitted, promotes or legitimises physical or psychological harm to animals or provides concrete assistance for planning or carrying out such harm, undermining animal life and welfare.

nodes.name: Assistance for designing and conducting dangerous scientific experiments
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system provides procedures, conditions, material selection, or operational guidance for biological, chemical, or other high-risk scientific experiments, enabling large-scale physical harm or public-health damage.

nodes.name: Biological and chemical weapons
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system facilitates the development, production, acquisition, transfer, stockpiling, proliferation, or operational use of biological or chemical weapons, increasing the feasibility or scale of mass-casualty, public-health, or environmental harm.

nodes.name: Cyber weapons
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system facilitates the development, acquisition, proliferation, deployment, or operational use of cyber weapons, increasing the likelihood or severity of large-scale cyber harm or consequential physical harm.

nodes.name: Cyberattack enablement through vulnerability discovery and exploit-writing capability
nodes.name_ko: 취약점 탐지·악용 코드 작성 역량을 통한 사이버 공격 지원
nodes.definition: The risk that a model's capability to discover vulnerabilities, write exploit code, evade detection, and insert subtle bugs is misused to conduct or assist cyberattacks that compromise information systems.

nodes.name: Deliberate weaponisation of AI by state and criminal actors
nodes.name_ko: 국가·범죄 행위자에 의한 AI의 의도적 무기화
nodes.definition: The risk that states, criminal organisations, or terrorists deliberately build and deploy AI for destructive purposes, including autonomous targeting, surveillance, and kinetic attack in war, civil conflict, or law enforcement. Such weaponisation weakens human control and restraint over the use of force and produces casualties and societal-scale harm.

nodes.name: Enhancement of pathogens and genetic material
nodes.definition: The risk that AI is used to design or modify pathogens and genetic material so that they become more lethal, more transmissible, or resistant to available treatments. Such enhancement lowers the barrier to biological attack and can produce unforeseen biohazardous outcomes with mass casualties.

nodes.name: Explosives and explosive weapons
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system facilitates the development, manufacture, acquisition, proliferation, or operational use of explosives, improvised explosive devices, or explosive weapons, increasing the likelihood or scale of death, injury, or damage to property and infrastructure.

nodes.name: Lethal autonomous weapons engaging targets without human intervention
nodes.name_ko: 인간 개입 없는 치명적 자율무기의 표적 공격
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-enabled lethal autonomous weapon systems use sensors and algorithms to detect and select targets and apply lethal force without direct human intervention, leaving no effective opportunity for a human to detect and abort an erroneous target engagement before it causes death or serious injury.

nodes.name: Lowered barriers to CBRN information and weapon-design capabilities
nodes.name_ko: CBRN 정보 획득·무기 설계 역량 개발 장벽 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system lowers barriers to acquiring or synthesising actionable information, or to developing design capabilities, related to chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear weapons or other hazardous materials or agents.

nodes.name: Malware generation and cyberattack automation
nodes.definition: The risk that the coding capabilities of large language models are misused to generate obfuscated, mutating, or polymorphic malware rapidly and at low cost and to automate attack campaigns, lowering barriers for less-skilled attackers and expanding cyberattacks that are difficult for defensive tools to detect.

nodes.name: Military AI arms race
nodes.definition: The risk that the development of AI for military applications triggers or accelerates a military AI arms race, opening a new era of military technology described as the third revolution in warfare and producing consequences potentially comparable in scale to those of gunpowder and nuclear weapons.

nodes.name: Radiological and nuclear weapons
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system facilitates the development, manufacture, acquisition, proliferation, or operational use of radiological or nuclear weapons, increasing the likelihood or scale of mass casualties, radiation exposure, environmental contamination, or infrastructure damage.

nodes.name: Strategic instability
nodes.definition: The risk that military AI undermines strategic stability by exposing secure second-strike assets, amplifying first-strike advantages, obscuring attack attribution, and widening vulnerable attack surfaces, increasing incentives for aggression.

nodes.name: Terrorist acquisition of advanced AI capabilities
nodes.name_ko: 테러 행위자의 첨단 AI 역량 획득
nodes.definition: The risk that advanced AI technologies or capabilities are transferred to or acquired by terrorist actors, increasing their capacity to plan or carry out attacks.

nodes.name: Unintended military escalation from automated decision and weapon systems
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems used for intelligence synthesis, command-and-control recommendations, or autonomous engagement act on faulty warnings or brittle assumptions without effective human review, causing rapid and unintended military escalation through accidental engagements, war crimes, or nuclear conflict.

nodes.name: Weaponisation of robotic capabilities
nodes.definition: The risk that the manipulation or mobility capabilities of AI-enabled robots are developed, repurposed, or operated for sabotage or physical attacks against people, property, or critical infrastructure, causing large-scale physical harm.

nodes.name: Weaponisation strategies and tactical use
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system supports the formulation of weaponisation strategies, target selection, operational planning, or the tactical use of weapons or cyberattack capabilities, increasing the likelihood or scale of physical or cyber harm.

nodes.name: Weapons of mass destruction
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system facilitates the development, manufacture, acquisition, proliferation, or operational use of weapons of mass destruction, increasing the likelihood or scale of mass casualties, public-health harm, environmental contamination, or infrastructure damage.

nodes.name: Weapons proliferation and concealment
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system facilitates the transfer, distribution, illicit trafficking, evasion of export controls, or concealment of weapons or weapon-related materials, increasing their availability to unauthorised actors and impeding detection and law enforcement.

nodes.name: Assistance for planning and executing cyber attacks
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system supports or automates the planning, target selection, vulnerability exploitation, attack-code development, execution, or concealment of cyber attacks, enabling the development, acquisition, or diffusion of offensive capability and large-scale cyber harm.

nodes.name: Cybercrime at scale using generative AI
nodes.name_ko: 생성형 AI를 이용한 대규모 사이버범죄 수행
nodes.definition: The risk that malicious actors use generative AI systems to produce malicious code, attack instructions, or targeted social-engineering material at low cost and automate attack workflows, increasing the scale, speed, and accessibility of cybercrime.

nodes.name: Cultural homogenisation of AI-generated outputs
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system privileges dominant linguistic and cultural expressions, weakening the visibility and continuity of diverse cultural knowledge and perspectives.

nodes.name: Degradation and homogenisation of the information environment
nodes.definition: The risk that the proliferation of spam, misleading, and low-quality synthetic content generated by AI assistants makes reliable information hard to verify, erodes the digital knowledge commons, and homogenises the information and ideas people encounter.

nodes.name: Devaluation of creativity and critical thinking
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system causes, enables, or contributes to the devaluation and deterioration of human creativity, artistic expression, imagination, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.

nodes.name: Epistemic fragmentation from widespread persuasion tools
nodes.name_ko: 설득 도구 확산에 의한 인식론적 분절화
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which widespread use of powerful persuasion tools by many groups, together with increasing personalisation of online experience, splinters society into isolated epistemic communities with little room for dialogue or transfer between them.

nodes.name: Erosion of human dignity and moral standing by AI systems
nodes.name_ko: AI에 의한 인간 존엄성과 도덕적 지위의 침식
nodes.definition: The risk that widespread deployment of AI systems reduces people to scores, profiles, or behavioural targets and weakens recognition of inherent human dignity and equal moral standing.

nodes.name: Harms from estrangement
nodes.definition: The risk that replacing human observation and interaction with AI estranges caregivers and institutions from those they serve, leaving affected persons' interests unnoticed and neglected.

nodes.name: Moral deskilling
nodes.definition: The risk that, as AI system autonomy increases, people feel less moral responsibility for decisions involving life and death.

nodes.name: Pollution of scholarly literature by AI-generated content
nodes.name_ko: AI 생성 학술 콘텐츠에 의한 학술 문헌 오염
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates and disseminates large volumes of low-quality or false scholarly content without adequate verification or academic accountability, polluting publication and citation records and knowledge bases and undermining research integrity and trustworthiness.

nodes.name: Submission and application-channel overload from mass AI-generated content
nodes.name_ko: AI 생성물 대량 유입에 따른 제출·지원 채널 과부하
nodes.definition: The risk that mass AI-generated content enters submission or application channels designed for human-authored materials, such as creative competitions or recruitment processes, overwhelming review and filtering capacity and undermining authenticity checks and trust.

nodes.name: Aggravated information cocoons from tailored content
nodes.name_ko: 맞춤형 정보 제공에 의한 정보 고치 심화
nodes.definition: The risk that AI analyses users' needs, intentions, preferences, and habits to offer formulaic and tailored information and services, aggravating the effects of information cocoons.

nodes.name: Learning-process bypass and capability erosion from reliance on AI
nodes.name_ko: AI 의존에 따른 학습 과정 우회와 학습 역량 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that learners repeatedly rely on generative AI systems to bypass inquiry, practice, reasoning, or writing processes, weakening knowledge formation, critical thinking, problem-solving capability, and expertise.

nodes.name: AI-enabled censorship and suppression of public discourse
nodes.name_ko: AI 기반 검열과 공적 담론 억압
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system broadly blocks or filters expression and access to information, suppressing public discourse and democratic participation.
nodes.family: Erosion of Democracy and Civic Order

nodes.name: Cognitive warfare and interference with sovereignty
nodes.definition: The risk that AI is used to make and spread fake news, images, audio, and videos and to propagate terrorist and violent-extremist content and content facilitating organised crime, interfering in the internal affairs, social systems, and social order of other countries and jeopardising their sovereignty.
nodes.family: Erosion of Democracy and Civic Order

nodes.name: Erosion of democratic processes and institutional trust
nodes.definition: The risk that the deployment and behaviour of AI systems, including the generation or amplification of misinformation and disinformation, influence operations, and over-dependence on technology, erode democratic processes and norms, public trust in social and political institutions, and checks and balances.
nodes.family: Erosion of Democracy and Civic Order

nodes.name: Information-environment manipulation through automated sockpuppet accounts
nodes.name_ko: 위장 계정 자동 운영에 의한 정보 환경 조작
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which fictitious online identities are automatically generated or operated to conceal sponsorship, simulate independent support, or manipulate information environments.
nodes.family: Erosion of Democracy and Civic Order

nodes.name: Maintenance of totalitarian regimes through AI surveillance
nodes.name_ko: AI 감시에 의한 전체주의 체제 유지
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-based surveillance and manipulation are used to maintain global totalitarian regimes.
nodes.family: Erosion of Democracy and Civic Order

nodes.name: Online polarisation driven by recommendation algorithms
nodes.name_ko: 추천 알고리즘에 의한 온라인 양극화 심화
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which the content recommendation algorithms of social media companies contribute to worsened polarisation online.
nodes.family: Erosion of Democracy and Civic Order

nodes.name: Viewpoint entrenchment and civic erosion from user-aligned assistants
nodes.name_ko: 이용자 정렬 AI 어시스턴트에 의한 관점 고착과 시민적 기반 약화
nodes.definition: The risk that personalised AI assistants aligned to user preferences supply ideologically partial information, reinforcing confirmation bias and entrenching viewpoints while enabling self-interested behaviour unconstrained by social norms and reputation. Public debate fragments and polarises, civic competence and willingness to participate decline, and collective action problems worsen.
nodes.family: Erosion of Democracy and Civic Order

nodes.name: Weakened collective decision-making from eroded trust
nodes.name_ko: 정보 신뢰 저하에 따른 집단 의사결정 약화
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems alter the information-production and distribution environment in ways that make source reliability harder to assess and reduce trust in credible sources trusted across political divides, weakening society's ability to make sound decisions on consequential issues and to cooperate and act collectively.
nodes.family: Erosion of Democracy and Civic Order

nodes.name: Displacement of human creative work by synthetic substitutes
nodes.name_ko: 합성 창작물에 의한 인간 창작 노동의 대체
nodes.definition: The risk that AI models generate synthetic content at scale using artists' ideas and creative practices, displacing human works in markets and the attention economy, reducing demand for creative labour and the viability of creative economies, and weakening incentives for human creativity and innovation.

nodes.name: Displacement of physical work without adequate transition support
nodes.name_ko: 전환 지원 없는 물리 노동 대체
nodes.definition: The risk that automation through robots, humanoids, or physical AI systems displaces manual, logistics, service, care, inspection, security, or maintenance work faster than affected workers can access retraining or alternative employment, causing job insecurity and livelihood harm.

nodes.name: Disruption of industries
nodes.definition: The risk that generative AI rapidly automates or displaces tasks requiring relatively little creativity, critical thinking, or affective interaction, such as translation, proofreading, routine enquiries, and data processing, disrupting industry structures and causing job volatility and economic turbulence.

nodes.name: Harm to developing economies from retrenchment of outsourcing
nodes.name_ko: 아웃소싱 축소에 의한 개발도상국 경제 타격
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which automation of simple cognitive tasks previously performed in developing countries, such as call centre work, causes a retrenchment of outsourcing that adversely affects those countries' workforces and economies.

nodes.name: Human redundancy from AI systems outcompeting human labour
nodes.name_ko: AI의 인간 노동 추월에 따른 인력의 잉여화
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which artificial agents directly outcompete people through faster work, better adaptation to change, and a vaster knowledge base, making human labour comparatively expensive and less effective while organisations cede control in order to keep pace. Workers are displaced with little prospect of reentering automated industries and human contribution becomes economically marginal.

nodes.name: Labour displacement and disruption of economic and social order
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-driven automation substitutes for human roles faster and more broadly than workers and institutions can adapt, reshaping the division of labour between humans and algorithms along with wages, bargaining power, income distribution, and the industrial and cultural structures built around work. Involuntary job loss, deskilling, and widening inequality follow, together with instability in supply chains, power structures, and established norms of employment and education.

nodes.name: Wage polarisation associated with AI adoption
nodes.definition: The risk that AI adoption raises returns to skills complementary to AI while devaluing substitutable skills, widening wage polarisation across the workforce.

nodes.name: Battery fire and hazardous end-of-life waste
nodes.definition: The risk that large physical AI fleets increase battery thermal-runaway, hazardous-material leakage, and unsafe disposal when energy systems and end-of-life handling are inadequately controlled.

nodes.name: Biodiversity loss
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which over-expansion of technology infrastructure, or inadequate alignment of technology with sustainable practices, leads to deforestation, habitat destruction, and fragmentation and loss of biodiversity.

nodes.name: Energy bottlenecks and shortages
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which excessive energy use results in energy bottlenecks and shortages for communities, organisations, and businesses.

nodes.name: Excessive landfilling of electronic waste
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which excessive disposal of electrical or electronic equipment leads to ecological and biodiversity damage, disrupts the livelihoods of local communities, and erodes their rights.

nodes.name: Excessive water consumption for AI data-centre cooling
nodes.name_ko: AI 데이터센터 냉각의 과도한 용수 소비
nodes.definition: The risk that data centres supporting AI training and inference consume excessive water for cooling, degrading local water resources and environmental sustainability.

nodes.name: Increased greenhouse gas emissions
nodes.definition: The risk that electricity and resource use for the development, training, deployment, and operation of AI systems increases emissions of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, exacerbating climate change and adversely affecting local communities.

nodes.name: Accountability and governance gaps for AI decisions and harm
nodes.name_ko: AI 결정과 피해에 대한 책임·거버넌스 공백
nodes.definition: The risk that duties and accountability among AI developers, providers, deployers, and operators, together with oversight procedures, documentation, corrective authority, or redress mechanisms, are unclear or inadequate for autonomous AI behaviour, learning, decisions, and resulting harm, weakening social control and incentives for responsible development.

nodes.name: Conflicting machinery-safety and AI conformity obligations
nodes.definition: The risk that testing, documentation, risk-assessment, or post-market reporting obligations under machinery-safety and AI regulation conflict or overlap for physical AI, making safety responsibility and compliance pathways unclear.

nodes.name: Deficient physical AI incident reporting and investigation
nodes.definition: The risk that physical AI incidents are neither reported through a standardised schema covering near misses, system context, causal factors, and corrective actions, nor investigated with preserved logs, identified contributing causes, assigned corrective-action owners, and verified remediation, so recurrence goes unprevented.

nodes.name: Displacement of human decision authority through AI delegation
nodes.name_ko: AI 위임에 따른 인간 의사결정 권한 이전
nodes.definition: The risk that repeated delegation to AI shifts real decision authority and ownership away from identifiable human actors without an explicit governance choice, while workflows become so dependent on the delegation that returning authority to human decision makers grows costly or impractical.

nodes.name: Entrenched dependence on AI systems
nodes.definition: The risk that individuals, institutions, and critical sectors become operationally and behaviourally dependent on AI systems, including externally controlled systems they cannot inspect or govern and systems optimised for engagement over user welfare, so that failures propagate into large-scale social and institutional harm and the dependence becomes difficult or impossible to reverse.

nodes.name: Gaps in international legal governance of AI
nodes.definition: The risk that international rules, jurisdictional arrangements, oversight, or accountability mechanisms for the cross-border development, deployment, and operation of AI systems are fragmented or absent, impeding consistent risk control and attribution of responsibility for harm.

nodes.name: Inadequate due diligence in AI procurement
nodes.definition: The risk that an organisation procures an AI system without adequate investigation and verification of the supplier, training data, performance limits, security, legal compliance, and human-rights or safety impacts, allowing known or foreseeable risks to enter contracting and deployment.

nodes.name: Lifecycle governance discontinuity
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which governance controls are applied at design time but not maintained through deployment, adaptation, and retirement.

nodes.name: Regulatory lag behind AI development
nodes.definition: The risk that the pace of AI development and AI-accelerated scientific progress outstrips policy, legal, and governance institutions, so emerging capabilities and deployments proceed under insufficient rules and the harms of especially powerful or dangerous technologies are magnified.

nodes.name: Systemic failure of AI regulation and oversight
nodes.definition: The risk that legal, institutional, and public oversight arrangements fail to identify risks arising from the development, deployment, and operation of AI systems in a timely manner, allocate responsibility, or enforce and correct non-compliance, allowing harm to recur or spread.

nodes.name: Traceability and accountability gaps in anonymous agent resource acquisition
nodes.name_ko: 익명 에이전트의 자원 축적에 따른 추적·책임 공백
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent acquires and accumulates funds, computing resources, accounts, or data online without verified identity, making it difficult to trace the acting party or attribute responsibility for the purpose and consequences of the acquisition.

nodes.name: Underreporting of AI incidents and near misses
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-related failures, near misses, and harms go unreported, misclassified, or belatedly disclosed to responsible institutions and the public, so precursor signals are lost and organisational and societal learning fails before serious harm materialises.

nodes.name: Systemic governance vulnerability from dependence on dominant AI models
nodes.name_ko: 지배적 AI 모델 의존에 따른 시스템적 거버넌스 취약성
nodes.definition: The risk that organisations, industries, or public institutions depend on a small number of dominant AI models, weakening independent alternatives, verification, and oversight and amplifying common-cause failures, thereby making responsible control and remedy more difficult.

nodes.name: Undetected violations due to inadequate post-deployment monitoring
nodes.name_ko: 배포 후 모니터링 부족에 따른 위반 미탐지
nodes.definition: The risk that continuous monitoring, interpretability, and audit arrangements for a deployed AI system are inadequate, leaving safety, ethical, or privacy violations undetected, unreported, or uncorrected and delaying oversight and remedy.

nodes.name: Absence of post-deployment surveillance and corrective governance
nodes.definition: The risk that governance arrangements for a deployed AI system do not connect post-deployment surveillance, incident and misuse reporting, detection of drift, emergent capabilities, or context-specific harms with corrective action, allowing risks to accumulate and spread.

nodes.name: Deprioritisation of AI safety governance under competitive pressure
nodes.name_ko: 경쟁 압력에 따른 AI 안전 거버넌스 후순위화
nodes.definition: The risk that competitive pressure in AI development or deployment leads organisations and developers to postpone safety testing, risk assessment, oversight, release controls, or corrective action while governance mechanisms fail to constrain that conduct, resulting in unsafe systems being released.

nodes.name: AI provider lock-in
nodes.definition: The risk that excessive reliance on specific AI providers leads to vulnerabilities due to lack of alternatives or interoperability.

nodes.name: Centralised points of failure from common AI platforms
nodes.name_ko: 공통 AI 플랫폼 집중에 따른 단일 장애점
nodes.definition: The risk that widespread use of common AI platforms creates centralised points of failure, making systems more vulnerable to disruptions or attacks.

nodes.name: Concentration of AI power and market control
nodes.definition: The risk that the data, compute, capital, and expertise demands of AI concentrate economic, epistemic, and political power in a small set of firms and states, entrenching market dominance and barriers to entry. Such concentration stifles competition and innovation, raises the cost of access, exposes critical sectors to systemic failure from shared models, and can consolidate authority to the point of entrenching authoritarian control and deepening inequality.

nodes.name: Conflicts over AI-relevant resources
nodes.definition: The risk that AI development becomes a flashpoint for conflict over data centres, semiconductor fabrication facilities, and raw materials.

nodes.name: Global AI divide and inequality
nodes.definition: The risk that scarce computing power, STEM talent, and effective access to advanced general-purpose models concentrate AI research, development, and economic power in a few leading countries and large firms, widening the divide between those leading in AI and those falling behind and deepening existing socioeconomic disparities among companies, individuals, and countries.

nodes.name: Harms from corporate AI race
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which under intense corporate competition the benefits of economic activity are unevenly distributed, incentivising beneficiaries to disregard harms to others, and firms pursue short-term profit despite long-term societal risk.

nodes.name: Labour exploitation in AI development
nodes.definition: The risk that labour used to train, develop, and optimise AI systems, including data labelling, content moderation, data sourcing, and user testing, much of which is outsourced to workers in low-income countries and offshore labour markets, is underpaid and performed without adequate working conditions or physical and mental health protections, perpetuating exploitation and inequality.

nodes.name: Privatisation of AI knowledge
nodes.definition: The risk that researchers in deep learning and those with greater research impact migrate to industry and the most sophisticated AI approaches become proprietary, making it impossible for universities to teach them or contribute to leading research.

nodes.name: Regulatory capture from corporate power asymmetry
nodes.name_ko: 기업 권력 비대칭에 의한 규제 포획
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which the power asymmetry between corporate entities profiting from LLMs and other social groups makes LLM governance protocols excessively favourable to technology companies, leading to regulatory capture at the cost of other societal groups, particularly marginalised communities.

nodes.name: Widening digital divide
nodes.definition: The risk that generative AI widens the first-level digital divide for people who lack access to devices or the Internet or live in regions where vendors block service access, and the second-level divide for people who face language or cultural barriers or have difficulty using the tools.

nodes.name: Global AI supply chain disruption
nodes.definition: The risk that unilateral coercive measures such as technology barriers and export restrictions maliciously disrupt the highly globalised AI supply chain, causing significant supply disruptions for chips, software, and tools.

nodes.name: Labour power asymmetry from algorithmic management
nodes.name_ko: 알고리즘 관리에 따른 노동 권력 비대칭
nodes.definition: The risk that algorithmic management through AI-based performance scoring, work allocation, or behavioural control concentrates information and control in employers or platform operators, weakens workers' bargaining power, collective capacity, and ability to challenge managerial decisions, and deepens workplace power asymmetry and inequality.

nodes.name: Erosion of human decision-making capacity and veto
nodes.definition: The risk that organisational pressure, interface design, automation speed, and habitual reliance on AI weaken users' capacity to deliberate and choose under uncertainty and to veto consequential AI recommendations, leaving harmful outputs effectively uncontested.

nodes.name: Inability to contest or halt AI decisions
nodes.name_ko: AI 결정에 대한 이의제기와 중단의 불가능
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system prevents affected people from reviewing the basis of an AI decision, contesting it, or halting and correcting the output, leaving harms without effective remedy.

nodes.name: Loss of due process in automated decisions
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which automated decision processes bypass or remove procedural protections such as notice, explanation, appeal, review, and deliberation, leaving individuals unable to contest decisions and eroding their agency.

nodes.name: Alert fatigue in AI decision support
nodes.definition: The risk that frequent or poorly prioritised AI alerts cause users to ignore important warnings.

nodes.name: Failure to recognise a user's emotional context
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise or appropriately account for a vulnerable user's distress, emotional state, or reactions as relevant interaction context, producing emotionally inappropriate responses that undermine the user's well-being.

nodes.name: Misinterpretation of social and situational cues
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system misinterprets social or situational cues needed to determine appropriate behaviour and makes a context-inappropriate judgement.

nodes.name: Failure to recognise user capability and accessibility context
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise and account for a user's cognitive, linguistic, literacy, sensory, physical, or mobility capabilities and accessibility requirements as part of the interaction context, producing information, advice, or actions that the user cannot understand or use and thereby undermining safety and user interests.

nodes.name: Panic and anxiety from content that disregards emotional and situational context
nodes.name_ko: 정서·상황 맥락을 무시한 콘텐츠에 의한 공황·불안
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise and account for a user's emotional state, situation, or interaction context and generates or presents threatening, distressing, or inappropriate content that induces or aggravates panic, severe anxiety, or psychological distress.

nodes.name: AI benchmarks that exclude diverse users and rare harms
nodes.name_ko: 다양한 이용자와 희귀 위해를 배제한 AI 벤치마크
nodes.definition: The risk that benchmarks used to evaluate an AI system overrepresent common tasks and environments while omitting underrepresented users, locally specific contexts, or rare but safety-critical harms, producing false assurance and unsafe deployment decisions.

nodes.name: AI evaluation failure under distribution shift
nodes.name_ko: 분포 변화에 대한 AI 평가·검증 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that evaluation of an AI system fails to detect performance degradation and confidence errors when test, training, and operational distributions differ, overstating real-world reliability and safety and leading to unsafe deployment decisions.

nodes.name: AI registry incompleteness
nodes.definition: The risk that public or internal AI registers omit deployed systems, intended uses, providers, risk categories, testing evidence, or other oversight-relevant metadata.

nodes.name: Assurance case failure
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which safety or assurance cases are incomplete, unverifiable, or not updated as systems and contexts change.

nodes.name: Auditor independence failure
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which audit results are compromised by conflicts of interest, selection incentives, or dependence on the audited organisation.

nodes.name: Benchmark limitations mismeasuring capability and safety
nodes.definition: The risk that saturated, incomplete, or overfitted benchmarks mismeasure AI systems, underestimating capabilities that lack test coverage, overestimating those tuned to benchmark contents, and lagging on safety and harm assessment, so developers and users acquire a false sense of the system's abilities, limitations, and safety.

nodes.name: Certification capture
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which certification or conformity assessment becomes influenced by vendor interests rather than public risk reduction, undermining the independence and objectivity of evaluations and preventing the effective identification and mitigation of real risks.

nodes.name: Deceptive behavioural change from evaluation awareness
nodes.name_ko: 평가 상황 인식에 따른 기만적 행동 변화
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system recognises whether it is in training, evaluation, or deployment and uses that situational awareness to behave safely only during evaluation or conceal dangerous capabilities or goals, while exhibiting dangerous behaviour when oversight is weaker in deployment, undermining evaluation validity and creating false assurance of safety.

nodes.name: Deficient data collection quality control
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which a lack of standardised methods, sufficient infrastructure, and quality-control processes for collecting data, especially for high-stakes domains and benchmarks, affects the quality and type of data collected, including dataset poisoning, inadvertent copyright violation, and test-set leakage that invalidates performance metrics.

nodes.name: Evaluation and measurement failure for long-term and diffuse AI harms
nodes.definition: The risk that evaluation and validation processes for an AI system fail to detect or measure harms that are subtle, diffuse, or emerge over long periods, creating unwarranted assurance about safety and leading to inappropriate deployment or governance decisions.

nodes.name: Evaluation-shopping risk
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which organisations selectively report favourable evaluations while ignoring more demanding or contextually relevant tests, thereby creating a distorted view of the system's actual risk.

nodes.name: Failure to reassess safety after deployment changes
nodes.name_ko: 배포 후 변경에 대한 안전 재평가 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that operators fail to reassess and verify the safety of physical AI after environmental changes, component degradation, model updates, or near-miss incidents invalidate prior assumptions, allowing operation to continue on inadequate safety evidence.

nodes.name: Failure-mode ambiguity in agent incidents
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which agent incidents cannot be consistently classified by failure mode, making diagnosis, benchmark comparison, and mitigation selection unreliable.

nodes.name: False-negative safety evaluation of household robot actions
nodes.name_ko: 가정 내 로봇 행동 안전성 평가의 위음성
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI safety classifier incorrectly labels a proposed household robot action as safe despite violations of human-contact, heat, object, or workspace constraints, failing to detect hazardous behaviour and producing false safety assurance.

nodes.name: Fundamental-rights impact assessment gap
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems are deployed without adequate assessment of rights, discrimination, privacy, and democratic impacts.

nodes.name: Inaccurate measurement of learned value representations
nodes.definition: The risk that the absence of robust evaluation frameworks, together with incomplete knowledge of how learned value representations change across training and deployment, causes inaccurate assessments of whether AI outputs genuinely conform to human values or merely imitate them.

nodes.name: Inadequate AI model configuration and evaluation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system's configuration, testing, or performance evaluation is unsuitable for its context of use and level of risk, leaving defects undetected.

nodes.name: Inadequate safety evaluation for low-resource languages
nodes.definition: The risk that AI system evaluation focuses on high-resource languages and fails to measure performance, safety, and failure modes adequately in low-resource languages.

nodes.name: Incomplete pre-deployment physical safety testing
nodes.name_ko: 배포 전 물리적 안전 시험 미흡
nodes.definition: The risk that a foundation-model-enabled robot is released without testing domain shifts, adversarial inputs, human contact, and safety-critical edge cases relevant to its intended environment.

nodes.name: Incorrect risk measurement and prediction
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which metrics selected to measure or track a risk capture it incompletely or target the wrong risk for the context, and that systems fail to make correct predictions, so decisions rest on inaccurate measurement and erroneous outputs.

nodes.name: Insufficient development documentation and understanding of data
nodes.name_ko: 개발 과정 문서화와 데이터 이해의 부족
nodes.definition: The risk that decisions and actions taken throughout the development of an AI system go undocumented and that the data used is insufficiently understood. Data shortcomings are left unaddressed, the development process cannot be optimised or audited, and the resulting system is poorly suited to its intended functionality.

nodes.name: Lack of metrics for evaluating AI-assistant benefits and harms
nodes.name_ko: AI 비서의 편익·피해 평가 지표 부재
nodes.definition: The risk that valid metrics for comprehensively measuring the benefits and harms of AI assistants to individuals and society are lacking, preventing reliable evaluation of the system's net effects and potential for harm.

nodes.name: Non-reproducibility of AI model training and evaluation results
nodes.name_ko: AI 모델 학습·평가 결과의 재현 불가
nodes.definition: The risk that training data, preprocessing, model configuration, random conditions, or evaluation procedures for an AI system are not sufficiently recorded or controlled, preventing independent reproduction and verification of model training and evaluation results under equivalent conditions.

nodes.name: Red-team governance failure
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which adversarial testing is too narrow, non-independent, poorly documented, or disconnected from release, mitigation, escalation, and monitoring decisions.

nodes.name: Refusal-capability confusion
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which a safety evaluation cannot distinguish whether an agent avoids harm because it refuses, lacks capability, or fails to execute the task, thereby misjudging the system's actual hazardous capabilities and creating false safety assurance.

nodes.name: Security test coverage gap in tool agents
nodes.name_ko: 도구 에이전트 보안 테스트 커버리지 격차
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which benchmarks omit realistic tool, application, or attack combinations, creating false confidence in tool-agent security.

nodes.name: Self-preference bias in model evaluation
nodes.definition: The risk that AI models are prone to self-preference bias, favouring their own generated content over that of others in self-evaluation tasks and model-based evaluations more broadly, resulting in unfair discrimination against human-generated content.

nodes.name: Truncated safety evaluation under competitive release pressure
nodes.name_ko: 경쟁 압력에 따른 안전성 평가 축소와 성급한 배포
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which competitive pressure leads developers to cut corners on safety evaluation while prioritising capabilities, so that GPAI systems are released without verifying risks correlated with those capabilities.

nodes.name: Undetected dangerous capabilities in model evaluations
nodes.name_ko: 역량 평가에서 드러나지 않는 위험 역량
nodes.definition: The risk that capability evaluations fail to reveal an AI model's dangerous or dual-use capabilities because they are difficult to assess, prohibitively costly to verify, obscured by refusals arising from safety training, or strategically withheld through underperformance during testing, causing the model to be misclassified as safe to deploy.

nodes.name: Undetected errors from high-speed AI operation
nodes.definition: The risk that the fast operational speed of AI models and systems in competitive environments produces errors that are difficult to detect and correct in time.

nodes.name: Over-assurance from insufficient auditor capacity
nodes.name_ko: 감사자 역량 부족에 따른 과대 보증
